```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Detach all clients of the current tmux session, then destroy the session.
3	# Gives "kill current session and return to parent shell" behavior even
4	# when `detach-on-destroy off` is set globally (common.conf), which would
5	# otherwise make `kill-session` switch to another session instead.
6	set -euo pipefail
7	
8	session=$(tmux display-message -p '#S')
9	tmux detach-client -s "$session"
10	tmux kill-session -t "$session"
11
```
</details></tool-use>

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-14 12:55:20Z)**_

找到根因了。`dot_config/tmux/common.conf.tmpl:16` 有 `set -g @continuum-restore 'on'` — tmux-continuum 每 15 分鐘存一次快照到 `~/.local/share/tmux/resurrect/last`,然後**每次 tmux server 啟動時無條件 auto-restore**,它沒辦法分辨「主動 `kill-server`」vs「crash / reboot」,看起來都是「server 不在了 → 還原」。

幾種解法,差別在你多常想要 auto-restore vs clean start:

| 方案 | 改動 | 適合什麼場景 |
|---|---|---|
| **A. 關掉 auto-restore,改手動** | 拿掉 `@continuum-restore 'on'`(periodic save 保留),需要時 `prefix + Ctrl-r` 手動 restore | 多數時候想 clean start,只在 reboot/crash 後手動撈 |
| **B. 保留 auto-restore,提供一個「乾淨退出」wrapper** | 新增 script:刪 `~/.local/share/tmux/resurrect/last` 再 `kill-server`(綁個 keybinding 或 alias 如 `tmux-quit-clean`) | 平常想 auto-restore,只有「我今天工作做完了」時才要 clean |
| **C. 不存 = 不還原** | 拿掉 continuum-restore + 把 `@continuum-save-interval` 設 `0` 停止 periodic save,完全靠 `prefix + Ctrl-s` 手動存 | 你根本不太用 restore,只是當保險絲 |
| **D. 維持現狀,知道訣竅** | 主動 kill 前先 `rm ~/.local/share/tmux/resurrect/last`,或 `kill-server` 後再刪一次 | 不想動 config |

我的傾向是 **B**(保留 auto-restore 的好處,但給你一個明確的「我是故意關掉的」出口),而且這個 repo 已經有 `kill-session-exit.sh` 的前例可以加一個 `kill-server-clean.sh` 進去。

你想走哪一條?(或要不要我直接幫你實作 B?)

## TMUX Mouse-Menu & Session-Killing Inventory

### 1. **TMUX MOUSE RIGHT-CLICK MENUS**

**MouseDown3Pane** (`keybindings.conf.tmpl:19-46`)
- Right-click on a pane opens a menu with:
  - Split/swap/resize/zoom options
  - **Kill pane**: `confirm-before -p "Kill pane? (y/n)" kill-pane`
- Uses `-O` flag to keep menu open until selection

**MouseDown3Status** (`keybindings.conf.tmpl:48-92`)
- Right-click on a window tab opens a menu with:
  - Layout selection (even-horizontal, main-vertical, tiled, etc.)
  - **Kill window**: `kill-window` (no confirm)
  - Window renumbering, renaming, bookmarking (⭐/📌/🔖/🚩)
- Note: 23 visible rows; silently suppresses on small terminals (<14 rows)

**MouseDown3StatusLeft** (`keybindings.conf.tmpl:94-110`)
- Right-click on session name area (left status) opens a menu with:
  - Session switcher (next/previous/choose)
  - **Kill session**: `kill-session`
  - **Kill session & exit**: `run-shell "~/.config/tmux/kill-session-exit.sh"`

### 2. **SESSION/WINDOW/PANE KILL PATHS**

**Prefix Keybindings** (`keybindings.conf.tmpl:276-286`):
- `prefix + X` → `kill-session` (switch to another session, don't exit)

- `prefix + x` → `confirm-before "Kill pane? (y/n)" kill-pane`
- `prefix + W` → `confirm-before "Kill window #W? (y/n)" kill-window`

**Helper Script** (`executable_kill-session-exit.sh:1-11`):
```bash

# Detach all clients of the current tmux session, then destroy the session.

tmux kill-session -t "$session"

## TMUX KEYBOARD-SHORTCUT NAMESPACE SURVEY

### 1. Prefix vs Root-Table Policy

**Policy statement**: CLAUDE.md line 24 establishes the convention:
> "Keybinding (`Ctrl+`/`Alt+`) in any tool config — Cross-check namespace before claiming — **tmux root-table `bind -n C-*` shadows inner apps; prefer `Alt+` for new actions**"

**Established convention** (from `common.conf.tmpl` and `keybindings.conf.tmpl`):
- **Prefix + letter bindings** are the primary namespace for interactive menu actions and session management
- **Root-table `C-<key>` bindings** are reserved for window switching (`C-1..9`, `C-0`) and vim-pane navigation (`C-h/j/k/l`). These **shadow inner apps intentionally** because they cross into Neovim/vim splits.
- **Root-table `M-<key>` (Alt) bindings** are preferred for menu-like actions that need to be accessible without prefix. Currently used for: layouts (`M-1..5`), resize (`M-h/j/k/l`), theme switching (`M-c`, `M-t`), copy operations (`M-y`, `M-i`), and help (`M-/`).

**Example existing bindings**:
- Prefix table: `prefix + g` (sesh picker), `prefix + G` (lazygit), `prefix + Space` (menu), `prefix + 0` (sesh-root), `prefix + 9` (scode)
- Root table: `C-1..9` (window switch), `C-0` (sesh-root), `C-h/j/k/l` (vim-tmux-navigator), `M-1..5` (layouts)

---

### 2. Currently Bound Keys — Complete Inventory

#### Prefix table (single-letter / punctuation bindings)
```
c  new-window             h/j/k/l  pane select (L/D/U/R)
y  copy visible pane      H/J/K/L  resize 5 cells (L/D/U/R)
Y  copy full scrollback   M-h/j/k/l  resize 1 cell (L/D/U/R)
C-y  copy fzf lines      |  split-window -h
M-y  copy last output     -  split-window -v
M-i  copy last input      +  resize 75% width
r  renumber windows       ?  tmux-fzf keybinding picker
R  reload config         C-?  list-keys -N (fallback)
N  new session          M-/  cheatsheet popup
X  kill session         Space  menu.sh (main popup)
x  kill pane             `  one-shot shell popup
W  kill window           0  sesh-root (lightweight)
M-x  kill & exit tmux    9  scode (coding layout)

#### Root-table `bind -n C-<digit>` (window switching, CSI-u required)

C-0              sesh-root for current dir (mirrors prefix+0)
```

#### Root-table `bind -n C-<h/j/k/l>` (vim-tmux-navigator, gated on enableVimMode)
```
C-h  select pane L  (if not in vim; if in vim, send C-h to vim)
C-j  select pane D  (if not in vim; if in vim, send C-j to vim)
C-k  select pane U  (if not in vim; if in vim, send C-k to vim)
C-l  select pane R  (if not in vim; if in vim, send C-l to vim)
```

#### Root-table `bind -n M-<key>` (Alt bindings — Alt preferred for new actions)
```
M-1 through M-5  layouts (even-h, even-v, main-h, main-v, tiled)
M-h/j/k/l       fine resize 1 cell (L/D/U/R, repeatable)
M-c              catppuccin theme
M-t              tmux2k theme
M-x              kill session & exit tmux
M-y              copy last command output
M-i              copy last command input
M-/              cheatsheet popup
```

#### Root-table mouse bindings (right-click menus, always bound)
```
MouseDown3Pane       pane right-click menu (13 rows: split/swap/zoom/resize/mark/join/etc)
MouseDown3Status     window-tab right-click menu (23 rows: swap/layout/rename/bookmark/kill)
MouseDown3StatusLeft session-left right-click menu (11 rows: next/prev/rename/move-window)

### 3. Three Target Menu Trigger Lines

**Pane right-click menu** (`MouseDown3Pane`):
```
keybindings.conf.tmpl:20–46
unbind-key -n MouseDown3Pane
bind-key -n MouseDown3Pane \
  if-shell -F -t = "#{||:#{mouse_any_flag},#{&&:#{pane_in_mode},#{?#{m/r:(copy|view)-mode,#{pane_mode}},0,1}}}" \
    { select-pane -t = ; send-keys -M } \
    { display-menu -O -T "#[align=centre]#{pane_current_command} (pane #{pane_index})" -t = -x M -y M \
        "Horizontal Split" h { split-window -h -c "#{pane_current_path}" } \
        ...
```
**Trigger line (20–23)**: Detects mouse in copy-mode; if not, opens pane context menu at mouse position.

**Window-tab right-click menu** (`MouseDown3Status`):
```
keybindings.conf.tmpl:48–92
unbind-key -n MouseDown3Status
bind-key -n MouseDown3Status \
  display-menu -O -T "#[align=centre]#{window_index}:#{window_name}" -t = -x W -y W \
    "Swap Left"  l { swap-window -t :-1 } \
    ...
    "New window"  w { new-window }
```
**Trigger line (48)**: Status bar (tab bar) right-click opens window context menu.

**Session-status-left right-click menu** (`MouseDown3StatusLeft`):
```
keybindings.conf.tmpl:94–110
unbind-key -n MouseDown3StatusLeft
bind-key -n MouseDown3StatusLeft \
  display-menu -O -T "#[align=centre]#{session_name}" -t = -x M -y W \
    Next        n { switch-client -n } \
    ...
    "Kill all sessions"   Q { confirm-before -p "Kill ALL sessions (tmux server)? (y/n)" kill-server }
```
**Trigger line (94)**: Status-left area (session indicator) right-click opens session context menu.

129	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
130	# Command-boundary navigation in copy-mode (Warp-style).
131	# Requires OSC 133 markers from the shell — emitted by
132	# dot_config/zsh/tools/02_shell_integration.zsh. In a plain shell (no markers,
133	# e.g. `sh`, `bash` without our hook, or `DISABLE_OSC133=1`), these keys are
134	# no-ops. tmux 3.4+ required for next-prompt/previous-prompt; the `-o` variant
135	# (jump to output start, not prompt start) is tmux 3.5+.
136	#
137	#   {  / }    previous/next prompt (the prompt line itself)
138	#   M-[ / M-] previous/next command output (line AFTER the prompt — usually
139	#             what you want for "skip to the output of the previous command")
140	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
141	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} '{' send-keys -X previous-prompt
142	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} '}' send-keys -X next-prompt
143	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} M-[ send-keys -X previous-prompt -o

153	# over SSH without shelling out to pbcopy/xclip on the remote host.

165	# prefix + M-y: copy the LAST command's OUTPUT to clipboard (Warp-style).
166	# Requires OSC 133 markers — if the shell doesn't emit them (non-zsh shell,
167	# DISABLE_OSC133=1, or a remote bash without our hook), selection ends up
168	# empty. Chain: enter copy-mode, jump to start of previous command's output,
169	# begin selection, jump forward to the next prompt (end of output), copy,
170	# flash confirmation.
171	bind M-y copy-mode \; \
172	  send-keys -X previous-prompt -o \; \
173	  send-keys -X begin-selection \; \
174	  send-keys -X next-prompt \; \
175	  send-keys -X copy-pipe-and-cancel "tmux load-buffer -w -" \; \
176	  display-message "Last command output copied to clipboard"
177	
178	# prefix + M-i: copy the LAST command's INPUT LINE (prompt + typed command).
179	# Same dependency on OSC 133 markers. Because we don't emit the B marker
180	# (end-of-prompt), the copied text includes prompt chrome (e.g. "❯ echo hi"
181	# not just "echo hi"). Trim in the paste target if needed. Chain: enter
182	# copy-mode, jump to the previous prompt's A marker, begin selection, jump
183	# forward to the C marker (= start of output = end of input line), copy.
184	bind M-i copy-mode \; \
185	  send-keys -X previous-prompt \; \
186	  send-keys -X begin-selection \; \
187	  send-keys -X next-prompt -o \; \
188	  send-keys -X copy-pipe-and-cancel "tmux load-buffer -w -" \; \
189	  display-message "Last command input (prompt+line) copied to clipboard"
190	
191	# =============================================================================
192	# Vim-Style Pane Navigation
193	# =============================================================================
194	
195	bind h select-pane -L
196	bind j select-pane -D
197	bind k select-pane -U
198	bind l select-pane -R
199	
200	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
201	# vim-tmux-navigator: prefix-less Ctrl+h/j/k/l crosses tmux panes <-> vim splits
202	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
203	# Detect if the current pane is running vim/neovim; if so forward the key,
204	# otherwise move between tmux panes. Matches christoomey/vim-tmux-navigator.
205	# Gated on chezmoi `enableVimMode` (default true). When off, Ctrl+h/j/k/l
206	# pass through to the inner shell (Ctrl+L = clear, Ctrl+H = backspace, etc.).
207	# See docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md.
208	{{ if .enableVimMode -}}
209	is_vim="ps -o state= -o comm= -t '#{pane_tty}' | grep -iqE '^[^TXZ ]+ +(\\S+\\/)?g?\\.?(view|n?vim?x?)(-wrapped)?(diff)?$'"
210	bind-key -n 'C-h' if-shell "$is_vim" 'send-keys C-h'  'select-pane -L'
211	bind-key -n 'C-j' if-shell "$is_vim" 'send-keys C-j'  'select-pane -D'
212	bind-key -n 'C-k' if-shell "$is_vim" 'send-keys C-k'  'select-pane -U'
213	bind-key -n 'C-l' if-shell "$is_vim" 'send-keys C-l'  'select-pane -R'
214	# NOTE: C-\ (select-pane -l) removed — tmux 3.4+ cannot parse C-\ in config files.
215	# Use directional C-h/j/k/l instead, or prefix+; for last-pane.
216	
217	bind-key -T copy-mode-vi 'C-h' select-pane -L
218	bind-key -T copy-mode-vi 'C-j' select-pane -D
219	bind-key -T copy-mode-vi 'C-k' select-pane -U
220	bind-key -T copy-mode-vi 'C-l' select-pane -R
221	{{- else -}}
222	# enableVimMode = false: vim-tmux-navigator omitted. Use prefix + h/j/k/l
223	# (kept below) or prefix + Arrow for pane navigation.
224	{{- end }}
225	
226	# Intuitive split bindings (| = left/right, - = top/bottom)
227	bind | split-window -h -c "#{pane_current_path}"
228	bind - split-window -v -c "#{pane_current_path}"
229	
230	# Resize panes with prefix + H/J/K/L (5 cells)
231	bind -r H resize-pane -L 5
232	bind -r J resize-pane -D 5
233	bind -r K resize-pane -U 5
234	bind -r L resize-pane -R 5
235	
236	# Fine resize with Meta + h/j/k/l (1 cell, repeatable)
237	bind -r M-h resize-pane -L 1
238	bind -r M-j resize-pane -D 1
239	bind -r M-k resize-pane -U 1
240	bind -r M-l resize-pane -R 1
241	
242	# Quick ratio: set current pane to 75% width
243	bind + resize-pane -x 75%
244	
245	# =============================================================================
246	# Quick Window Switching (Ctrl+Number, requires CSI-u / extended-keys)
247	# =============================================================================
248	# Supplement to prefix + 1..9 (tmux built-in defaults, always available).
249	# These require extended-keys (CSI-u) support from the terminal emulator
250	# (Ghostty/cmux, Alacritty, Kitty, WezTerm). Legacy terminals (Terminal.app,
251	# plain SSH) will not send these sequences — use prefix + number instead.
252	# Note: prefix + 9 / prefix + 0 are rebound below (scode / sesh-root for
253	# current dir), so Ctrl+9 below is the only way to reach window 9 from
254	# the keyboard. Ctrl+0 mirrors prefix+0 (lightweight sesh-root) since
255	# base-index is 1 and window 0 doesn't exist.
256	
257	bind-key -n C-1 select-window -t :=1
258	bind-key -n C-2 select-window -t :=2
259	bind-key -n C-3 select-window -t :=3
260	bind-key -n C-4 select-window -t :=4
261	bind-key -n C-5 select-window -t :=5
262	bind-key -n C-6 select-window -t :=6
263	bind-key -n C-7 select-window -t :=7
264	bind-key -n C-8 select-window -t :=8
265	bind-key -n C-9 select-window -t :=9
266	bind-key -n C-0 run-shell -b "~/.config/tmux/sesh-root-here.sh '#{pane_current_path}'"
267	
268	# New window/pane inherits current path
269	bind c new-window -c "#{pane_current_path}"
270	
271	# Reload config with prefix + R
272	bind R source-file "$HOME/.tmux.conf" \; display-message "Sourced ~/.tmux.conf"
273	
274	# Session management
275	bind N command-prompt -p "New session:" "new-session -s '%%'"
276	bind X confirm-before -p "Kill session #S? (y/n)" kill-session
277	# Kill current session AND detach client (return to parent shell).
278	# Differs from `prefix + X` above, which keeps you inside tmux by
279	# switching to another session (detach-on-destroy off, common.conf).
280	# Chained via helper script because `confirm-before` takes a single
281	# tmux command; inline `\;` inside its string arg is not parsed as a
282	# command separator.
283	bind M-x confirm-before -p "Kill session #S and exit tmux? (y/n)" \
284	  "run-shell '$HOME/.config/tmux/kill-session-exit.sh'"
285	bind x confirm-before -p "Kill pane? (y/n)" kill-pane
286	bind W confirm-before -p "Kill window #W? (y/n)" kill-window
287	
288	# Manual renumber (renumber-windows on usually handles this, but kill-pane on
289	# multi-pane windows or shell-driven exits can leave gaps).
290	bind r move-window -r \; display-message "Windows renumbered"
291	
292	# =============================================================================
293	# Move/Break Windows Across Sessions (GUI tab tear-out feel)
294	# =============================================================================
295	# prefix + M : move current window to another session (interactive prompt).
296	#              Target form: "session:" (auto-pick index) or "session:index"
297	#              (use -k via "!session:index" trick? simpler: bare prompt).
298	#              Tab-completes existing sessions.
299	# prefix + B : break current pane into a new window AND move it to a target
300	#              session in one go (acts like dragging a tab out).
301	# prefix + A : link current window into another session (window appears in
302	#              both sessions; edit either, both update). Use prefix + & to
303	#              kill, or unlink-window to detach without killing.
304	#
305	# Cross-window pane operations (no top-level prefix binding — letter slots are
306	# saturated by resize-pane H/J/K/L and sesh-last S; pane join/send live in the
307	# right-click pane menu and the popup menu's Session submenu instead):
308	#   - Mark current pane:  prefix + m  (built-in)
309	#   - Pull marked pane:   right-click pane menu → "Join marked pane here"
310	#   - Push current pane:  right-click pane menu → "Send pane to..."
311	#   - Break out to new window: right-click pane menu → "Break to new window"
312	#                              or prefix + ! (built-in, same session)
313	#                              or prefix + B (break + move to chosen session)
314	
315	bind M run-shell "tmux set-environment -g _src_window '#{window_id}'" \; \
316	  display-message "Pick destination session to MOVE window into…" \; \
317	  choose-tree -Zs -F "#{session_name}" \
318	  "run-shell '~/.config/tmux/cross-session.sh move %%'"
319	bind B run-shell "tmux set-environment -g _src_pane '#{pane_id}'" \; \
320	  display-message "Pick destination session to BREAK pane into (as new window)…" \; \
321	  choose-tree -Zs -F "#{session_name}" \
322	  "run-shell '~/.config/tmux/cross-session.sh break %%'"
323	bind A run-shell "tmux set-environment -g _src_window '#{window_id}'" \; \
324	  display-message "Pick destination session to LINK window into (window lives in both)…" \; \
325	  choose-tree -Zs -F "#{session_name}" \
326	  "run-shell '~/.config/tmux/cross-session.sh link %%'"
327	
328	# prefix + E : explode — break EVERY pane in current window into its own window
329	#              within the SAME session. Use case: switching from wide screen
330	#              (multi-pane layout) to mobile/SSH where one pane per window is
331	#              easier than zooming with prefix + z. Source window keeps the
332	#              first pane; other panes become sibling windows inserted right
333	#              after it, named after each pane's current command.
334	bind E run-shell "~/.config/tmux/break-all-panes.sh"
335	
336	# =============================================================================
337	# Theme Switching (Catppuccin <-> tmux2k)
338	# =============================================================================
339	# Note: first-time switch requires `prefix + I` to install the target plugin.
340	
341	bind M-c run-shell "tmux set -g @theme_variant catppuccin; \
342	  tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf; \
343	  tmux display-message 'Theme: catppuccin'"
344	
345	bind M-t run-shell "tmux set -g @theme_variant tmux2k; \
346	  tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf; \
347	  tmux display-message 'Theme: tmux2k'"
348	
349	# =============================================================================
350	# Sesh (tmux session manager)
351	# =============================================================================
352	
353	# prefix + g: sesh picker in a tmux popup with fzf
354	bind-key "g" run-shell "sesh connect \"$(\
355	  sesh list --icons | fzf-tmux -p 80%,70% \
356	    --no-sort --ansi --border-label ' sesh ' --prompt '⚡  ' \
357	    --header '  ^a all ^t tmux ^g configs ^x zoxide ^d tmux kill ^f find' \
358	    --bind 'tab:down,btab:up' \
359	    --bind 'ctrl-a:change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
360	    --bind 'ctrl-t:change-prompt(🪟  )+reload(sesh list -t --icons)' \
361	    --bind 'ctrl-g:change-prompt(⚙️  )+reload(sesh list -c --icons)' \
362	    --bind 'ctrl-x:change-prompt(📁  )+reload(sesh list -z --icons)' \
363	    --bind 'ctrl-f:change-prompt(🔎  )+reload(fd -H -d 2 -t d -E .Trash . ~)' \
364	    --bind 'ctrl-d:execute(tmux kill-session -t {2..})+change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
365	    --preview-window 'right:55%' \
366	    --preview 'sesh preview {}' \
367	)\""
368	
369	bind -N "last-session (via sesh)" S run-shell "sesh last 2>/dev/null || tmux display-message 'No previous sesh session'"
370	
371	# prefix + 9: open repo-aware coding-agent layout (`scode`) for the current
372	# pane's directory. scode walks up from cwd to find .git; if not in a repo,
373	# the error surfaces in the tmux status line.
374	# Replaces the previous `sesh connect --root $(pwd)` binding (which had a
375	# subtle bug — $(pwd) was expanded once at config parse time, not per-press).
376	# Logic is in scode-here.sh because tmux run-shell is /bin/sh (can't see
377	# zsh functions) and the session-name + switch-client dance is non-trivial.
378	bind -N "scode for current dir (repo-aware coding layout)" 9 \
379	  run-shell -b "~/.config/tmux/scode-here.sh '#{pane_current_path}'"
380	
381	# prefix + 0: lightweight counterpart to prefix+9. Plain sesh session at
382	# the git root of the current pane's directory (no nvim/agent layout).
383	# Replaces tmux's built-in `select-window -t :=0` which always errored
384	# because base-index is 1 (no window 0 exists). Logic in sesh-root-here.sh
385	# — see that file for the two bugs in the original `sesh connect --root
386	# $(pwd)` binding (parse-time $(pwd) + misuse of --root flag).
387	bind -N "sesh-root for current dir (lightweight)" 0 \
388	  run-shell -b "~/.config/tmux/sesh-root-here.sh '#{pane_current_path}'"
389	
390	# prefix + T: sesh picker via television (tv) in a tmux popup
391	bind-key "T" display-popup -E -w 80% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' Sesh (tv) ' "tv sesh"
392	
393	# prefix + O: sesh built-in picker in a tmux popup
394	bind-key "O" display-popup -h 90% -w 50% -E "sesh picker -i"
395	
396	# prefix + U: CLI tools picker via television (tv tools)
397	bind-key "U" display-popup -E -w 80% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' CLI Tools (tv) ' "tv tools"
398	
399	# prefix + a: live coding-agent panes picker (tv agent-panes)
400	# Shows claude / cursor-agent / codex / opencode sessions currently running in
401	# any tmux pane. Enter switches focus to that pane. See:
402	#   docs/tools/agent-panes-discovery.md
403	bind-key "a" display-popup -E -w 80% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' Live agent panes (tv) ' "tv agent-panes"
404	
405	# (prefix + W is now bound earlier in this file as `kill-window`. The previous
406	# `sesh window` binding was removed because `sesh` has no `window` subcommand;
407	# pressing it printed sesh's help to a popup. See git history.)
408	
409	# =============================================================================
410	# Popup tools (display-popup -E -d '#{pane_current_path}')
411	# =============================================================================
412	# Floating scratch pane (tmux-floax) is on prefix + F (toggleable, persistent
413	# session named `float`). The bindings below are one-shot popups that close
414	# when the inner command exits — handy for "do one thing without disrupting
415	# the layout" workflows.
416	
417	# prefix + G: lazygit popup at current pane path
418	bind-key "G" display-popup -E -w 90% -h 90% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' lazygit ' "lazygit"
419	
420	# prefix + ` (backtick): one-shot popup shell at current pane path.
421	# Closes when the inner shell exits (`exit` or Ctrl-D). Each invocation gets
422	# a fresh shell — no state preserved. For a persistent scratchpad with
423	# history, use floax (prefix + F) instead.
424	bind-key '`' display-popup -E -w 80% -h 80% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' shell '
425	
426	# =============================================================================
427	# Help / cheatsheet
428	# =============================================================================
429	# tmux's built-in `prefix + ?` (list-keys -N) is hard to scan and can't search
430	# user-defined bindings well. We replace it with tmux-fzf's keybinding picker
431	# (fzf popup, fuzzy-searchable). The original list-keys is still reachable on
432	# `prefix + C-?` as a fallback.
433	#
434	# `prefix + /` (built-in: prompt for a key, show what it's bound to) is left
435	# alone — it's already useful for "what does THIS key do?" lookups.
436	#
437	# `?` inside the prefix + Enter popup menu opens a glow-rendered
438	# cheatsheet (curated, grouped, prettier than list-keys).
439	
440	unbind-key '?'
441	bind-key '?' run-shell -b "~/.tmux/plugins/tmux-fzf/main.sh"
442	bind-key 'C-?' list-keys -N
443	
444	# `/` inside the Enter-popup uses this; standalone prefix + / stays built-in
445	# (key-prompt). We expose the cheatsheet through the popup menu's `?` entry.
446	bind-key M-/ display-popup -E -w 80% -h 80% -T ' tmux cheatsheet ' \
447	  "glow -p ~/.config/tmux/cheatsheet.md 2>/dev/null \
448	    || less ~/.config/tmux/cheatsheet.md"
449	
450	# =============================================================================
451	# Popup Menu (prefix + Space)
452	# =============================================================================
453	# Two entry keys, same menu. The menu itself is generated by a script
454	# (`~/.config/tmux/menu.sh`) which:
455	#
456	#   1. Reads `#{client_height}` and emits a tier-trimmed row list. tmux's
457	#      `display-menu` does NOT paginate — if the menu is taller than the
458	#      terminal, the entire popup is silently suppressed (no error). The
459	#      script keeps the menu fitting on tiny mobile-SSH heights too.
460	#   2. Submenus are sibling scripts (menu-layouts.sh, menu-session.sh,
461	#      menu-sesh.sh, menu-popups.sh, menu-theme.sh, menu-system.sh). Each
462	#      `exec tmux display-menu …` so quoting context resets per submenu —
463	#      no nested-quote escaping disasters in keybindings.conf.
464	#
465	# History: an earlier flat ~50-row menu silently failed on smaller heights
466	# and was misdiagnosed as a csi-u key encoding bug, then as a quoting bug.
467	# Both real (the `\;` accelerator was broken, sesh fzf binds had nested-
468	# quote issues), but the dominant symptom — "menu doesn't open at all" —
469	# was actually menu-too-tall. See pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-parse-failure.md.
470	#
471	# Discovery fallbacks if you forget the keys: `prefix + ?` (tmux-fzf fuzzy
472	# picker over every binding), `prefix + M-/` (glow cheatsheet popup), or
473	# right-click on a pane / status line.
474	
475	unbind-key Space
476	unbind-key Enter
477	bind-key Space run-shell "~/.config/tmux/menu.sh"
478	# Note: `prefix + e` was previously a popup-menu alias (added as workaround
479	# for a misdiagnosed display-menu bug — see pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md).
480	# Removed so `e` is free as a sub-menu mnemonic (e.g. "Even layout: horizontal"
481	# in the window right-click menu).
482

117	
118	# Status-bar messages (display-message) — default 750ms is too short to read
119	# multi-word confirmations like "Moved to foo:3 (zsh)" before they vanish.
120	# 0 = stay until the next key event (the key still does its normal action;
121	# only the message gets cleared). Trade-off: occasionally a stale message
122	# lingers if you stop typing, but no important confirmation is ever missed.
123	set -g display-time 0
124	
125	# =============================================================================
126	# Terminal & Key Compatibility
127	# =============================================================================
128	
129	set -s default-terminal 'tmux-256color'
130	set -as terminal-features ",xterm-256color:RGB"
131	
132	# Forward extended keys (CSI-u) so Ctrl+/, Shift+Enter etc. reach TUIs.
133	#
134	# Use `on` (NOT `always`):
135	#   - `on`: emit CSI-u only when a key has NO legacy encoding (Shift+Enter,
136	#     Ctrl+Enter, Ctrl+/, Ctrl+digit). Keys with legacy encoding (Ctrl+letter
137	#     including Ctrl+J = LF, Ctrl+M = CR, Ctrl+I = TAB) keep their classic
138	#     bytes.
139	#   - `always`: emit CSI-u for EVERY modifier+key combo, including ones with
140	#     a legacy encoding. This breaks ble.sh paste handling because each `\n`
141	#     in pasted content gets re-encoded as `ESC[106;5u` (Ctrl+J as CSI-u),
142	#     and ble.sh inserts the escape sequence as literal text instead of as
143	#     a newline. See pitfalls/tmux-extended-keys-always-paste.md.
144	#
145	# Net result on `on`: TUIs that need Ctrl+Enter / Shift+Enter (Claude Code,
146	# Neovim, etc.) still get them; paste of multi-line text into ble.sh works
147	# correctly; legacy `Ctrl+letter` shortcuts in shells / tmux / TUIs keep
148	# their normal encodings.
149	set -s extended-keys on
150	if-shell 'tmux -V | grep -qE "tmux ([3-9]\.[5-9]|[3-9]\.[1-9][0-9]|[4-9]\.)"' \
151	  'set -s extended-keys-format csi-u'
152	set -as terminal-features 'xterm*:extkeys'
153	
154	# OSC 52 clipboard (works over SSH)
155	set -g set-clipboard on
156	
157	# Declare OSC 52 support explicitly for common outer terminals. tmux 3.2+ only
158	# emits OSC 52 when it believes the outer terminal supports it; most modern
159	# terminals (Ghostty, Alacritty, iTerm2, kitty, WezTerm) do. Without these
160	# hints tmux falls back to terminfo's `Ms` capability, which is absent from
161	# the `tmux-256color` entry shipped by many distros, so yanks from inner
162	# apps (e.g. Neovim over SSH) silently drop.
163	set -as terminal-features ",xterm*:clipboard"
164	set -as terminal-features ",ghostty*:clipboard"
165	set -as terminal-features ",alacritty*:clipboard"
166	
167	# Allow OSC passthrough (for terminal images, sixel, etc.)
168	set -g allow-passthrough on
169
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# Zsh Keybindings & the `keys-picker` Widget
2	
3	> **TL;DR** — press `Alt+/` in any zsh prompt to fuzzy-search every
4	> non-trivial keybinding (built-in, plugin, custom) with descriptions.
5	> Bash users (or scripts) can run `bindings` for the same data via `tv` /
6	> `bat` / `cat`. Source-of-truth markdown:
7	> [`dot_config/docs/shells/keybindings.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/docs/shells/keybindings.md)
8	> (deployed to `~/.config/docs/shells/keybindings.md`).
9	
10	For the **why** behind `Ctrl+A` / `Ctrl+E` / `Ctrl+W` / `Alt+.` etc. and
11	why every Unix shell shares them, see
12	[Emacs-style line editing — origin & the must-know subset](emacs-line-editing.md).
13	
14	---
15	
16	## Why this exists
17	
18	Zsh has no real `which-key` equivalent — that pattern needs a "leader key
19	+ timeout" mechanism (Vim's `<leader>`, tmux's `prefix`), and ZLE parses
20	keys eagerly, so a custom `Alt` keypress can never be made to "wait for
21	follow-up input". The pragmatic substitute is **a fzf picker that lists
22	every binding**, opened by a single hotkey.
23	
24	Three forgetfulness traps motivate it:
25	
26	1. **Custom `Alt+*` widgets in this repo** (`Alt+T` tools-picker,
27	   `Alt+S` sesh, `Alt+R` atuin, `Alt+P/G/E/A/I` television channels,
28	   `Alt+;` aisuggest, `Alt+/` keys-picker)
29	   — the namespace is dense; new widgets are forgotten within days.
30	2. **Plugin overrides** that shadow ZLE built-ins — e.g. `Ctrl+R` is no
31	   longer `history-incremental-search-backward`; on zsh it's
32	   `fzf-history-widget`, on bash it's atuin's TUI (asymmetric on purpose
33	   — see [atuin docs](../tools/atuin.md#keybindings-cross-shell-asymmetry--read-this)).
34	3. **Built-in editing shortcuts you rarely need until you do** —
35	   `Ctrl+X Ctrl+E` (open command in `$EDITOR`), `Alt+.` (insert last
36	   argument of previous command), `Ctrl+_` (undo).
37	
38	## Four layers of binding
39	
40	The cheatsheet is curated, not exhaustive — built-in / plugin rows are
41	selected for "frequently forgotten" rather than "every widget exists".
42	
43	| # | Layer | Source | Examples in cheatsheet |
44	|---|-------|--------|------------------------|
45	| 1 | **ZLE built-in** (emacs keymap) | Ships with zsh | `Ctrl+A`, `Ctrl+E`, `Ctrl+W`, `Alt+.`, `Ctrl+X Ctrl+E` |
46	| 2 | **OMZ / third-party plugins** | `dot_zshrc.tmpl:21-26` (`zsh-autosuggestions`, `zsh-syntax-highlighting`, `zsh-vi-mode`*) + fzf shell integration | `Ctrl+R` → fzf, `Ctrl+T` → fzf, `Alt+C` → fzf, `End` → autosuggest-accept |
47	| 3 | **Custom widgets in this repo** | `dot_config/zsh/tools/{05_aisuggest,11_tools_picker,12_television,22_sesh,13_keys_picker}.zsh` + `dot_config/shell/15_atuin.sh` | All `Alt+*` pickers + `Tab`/`→` aisuggest swap + `Alt+R` atuin |
48	| 4 | **Mode switches (vi)** | `zsh-vi-mode` plugin* | Intentionally **not listed** — `Esc` / `i` / `:` are mode transitions, not bindings |
49	
50	\* Conditional on the chezmoi `enableVimMode` prompt (default `true`).
51	When `false`, `zsh-vi-mode` is omitted from the OMZ plugin array and
52	mode switches go away. See [`docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md`](../this_repo/vim-mode.md)
53	for the full catalog of what changes.
54	
55	Layer 4 omitted on purpose (per the design spec): listing every
56	`vicmd`-mode key would balloon the picker to 200+ rows and dilute signal.
57	
58	## Three entry points
59	
60	| Method | Trigger | Where it works | Notes |
61	|--------|---------|----------------|-------|
62	| **ZLE picker** (canonical) | `Alt+/` | zsh interactive | Live `bindkey` lookup in preview; `Ctrl+E` triggers the widget directly; `Ctrl+L` swaps to raw `bindkey -M emacs` view (escape hatch for power users) |
63	| **Television channel** | `tv keybindings` | zsh & bash, any TTY | Same data source; `Enter` paste-comment, `Ctrl+Y` copy key combo |
64	| **Static viewer** | `bindings` | zsh & bash (POSIX function in `dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh`) | Picks `tv` → `bat` → `less` → `cat` in that order; safe in non-interactive `bash -c` too |
65	
66	The ZLE widget is rebound from `zvm_after_init` in
67	[`dot_zshrc.tmpl`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_zshrc.tmpl)
68	to survive `zsh-vi-mode`'s init-time keybind wipe — the same pattern as
69	`aisuggest`. Bash currently has no ZLE widget port; CLI fallback is
70	`bindings` (no ble.sh keybind because designing one duplicates the work
71	of [the planned bash `Alt+/` ble.sh binding](#future-bash-port)).
72	
73	## Picker keybindings (inside the fzf overlay)
74	
75	| Key | Action |
76	|-----|--------|
77	| `Enter` | Paste `# <key> → <widget>: <desc>` as a shell comment to the buffer (read-only result; press Enter again to noop, or `Ctrl+U` to discard) |
78	| `Ctrl+E` | Trigger the widget directly via `zle <widget-name>` (only works for widgets registered in current zsh; warns if not) |
79	| `Ctrl+L` | Reload picker with `bindkey -M emacs` raw output — the **escape hatch** for finding bindings the cheatsheet didn't curate |
80	| `Ctrl+/` | Toggle preview panel (live `bindkey` lookup + `grep` of the widget's source file in `~/.config/zsh/`) |
81	
82	## Format contract for the data source
83	
84	The data source [`dot_config/docs/shells/keybindings.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/docs/shells/keybindings.md)
85	is parsed by `awk -F'|'`. Every cheatsheet row MUST be exactly:
86	
87	```
88	| `<KEY>` | `<widget>` | <description> |
89	```
90	
91	Three pipe-delimited cells, key wrapped in backticks. Group headings
92	(`### …`) are valid markdown but skipped by the parser. Adding a fourth
93	column or unbalanced backticks **silently drops the row** — not a hard
94	error, but the row vanishes from the picker.
95	
96	The `tv keybindings` channel uses an embedded copy of the same awk
97	program — see
98	[`dot_config/television/cable/keybindings.toml`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/television/cable/keybindings.toml).
99	
100	## Maintenance rule
101	
102	Whenever you add, modify, or remove a custom zsh ZLE widget binding in
103	`dot_config/zsh/tools/*.zsh`, update **two** files in the same commit:
104	
105	1. [`dot_config/docs/shells/keybindings.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/docs/shells/keybindings.md) — the picker data source (one row per binding).
106	2. [`docs/shells/aliases.md`](aliases.md) — only if the change adds a
107	   user-callable function (`bindings`, `tools-picker` invoked manually).
108	   Pure ZLE widgets (`tv-files`, `keys-picker`) don't need an aliases.md row.
109	
110	This rule is also recorded in the cross-file maintenance section of
111	[`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/AGENTS.md).
112	
113	## Future: bash port {#future-bash-port}
114	
115	Bash has no equivalent of zsh ZLE widgets, but ble.sh's `ble-bind`
116	supports running a shell command on a key combo. A bash version of the
117	picker would:
118	
119	1. Live in `dot_config/bash/13_keys_picker.bash` (bash-only tier per the
120	   three-tier rule in `AGENTS.md`).
121	2. Use `ble-bind -f 'M-/' '_keys_picker_bash'` (Alt+/) inside
122	   `~/.bashrc.adhoc` (sourced after `ble-attach`).
123	3. Reuse the same data source and awk parser; just swap the action from
124	   `zle keys-picker` to a function that re-reads `READLINE_LINE` and
125	   `READLINE_POINT`.
126	
127	Deferred until there's a concrete bash-primary user need; see
128	[`backlog/`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/tree/main/backlog)
129	if it gets requested.
130	
131	## Related
132	
133	- [Emacs-style line editing — origin & must-know subset](emacs-line-editing.md) — the 1970s/80s history of why every Unix shell shares `Ctrl+A`/`Ctrl+E`/`Ctrl+W`/`Ctrl+R`, the kill-ring vs system clipboard distinction, and the recommended 8-key core for new users.
134	- [Aliases & functions](aliases.md) — sister cheatsheet for shell aliases (not keybindings).
135	- [Bash bootstrap](bash.md) — why bash needs `atuin init bash --disable-up-arrow` and how ble.sh fits in.
136	- [Architecture](architecture.md) — the shared / zsh-only / bash-only three-tier loader convention.
137
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# tmux — Keybindings
2	
3	All bindings use the default prefix `Ctrl + b`.
4	
5	## Daily Workflow
6	
7	| Keybinding | Action |
8	|------------|--------|
9	| `prefix + R` | Reload `~/.tmux.conf` |
10	| `prefix + Space` | Open the tmux popup menu (mnemonic: "menu") |
11	| `prefix + g` | Open sesh picker |
12	| `prefix + T` | Open sesh picker via television (tv) |
13	| `prefix + O` | Open sesh built-in picker |
14	| `prefix + S` | Jump to the last sesh session (status-bar message if none) |
15	| `prefix + 9` | Open `scode` for current dir (repo-aware coding-agent layout — nvim 75% \| agent 25% + btop monitor; idempotent, switches to existing session if already created) |
16	| `prefix + 0` | Lightweight sesh session at git root of current dir (no nvim/agent layout — symmetric counterpart to `prefix + 9`) |
17	| `prefix + N` | New session (prompts for name) |
18	| `prefix + X` | Kill session (with confirmation) |
19	| `prefix + W` | Kill window (with confirmation) |
20	| `prefix + r` | Renumber windows (close gaps left by killed windows) |
21	| `prefix + M` | Move current window to another session (prompts for `session[:index]`) |
22	| `prefix + B` | Break current pane into a new window and move it to a session (tab tear-out) |
23	| `prefix + A` | Link current window into another session (window appears in both) |
24	| `prefix + E` | Explode — break every pane in current window into its own window (same session). For switching from wide-screen multi-pane to mobile/SSH single-pane |
25	| `prefix + d` | Detach |
26	| `prefix + t` | Show tmux clock mode |
27	| `prefix + M-c` | Switch theme to Catppuccin (top status bar) |
28	| `prefix + M-t` | Switch theme to tmux2k (bottom status bar) |
29	
30	## Panes and Windows
31	
32	| Keybinding | Action |
33	|------------|--------|
34	| `Ctrl + 1..9` | Switch to window 1–9 (requires CSI-u terminal: Ghostty, Alacritty, Kitty) |
35	| `Ctrl + 0` | Lightweight sesh session at repo root for current pane (mirrors `prefix + 0`) |
36	| `Ctrl + h/j/k/l` | Move between panes — crosses into Neovim splits (vim-tmux-navigator)* |
37	| `Ctrl + \` | Focus previous pane/split (vim-tmux-navigator)* |
38	| `prefix + h/j/k/l` | Move between panes (fallback, tmux-only) |
39	| `prefix + H/J/K/L` | Resize panes (5 cells, repeatable) |
40	| `prefix + M-h/j/k/l` | Fine resize panes (1 cell, repeatable) |
41	| `prefix + +` | Set current pane to 75% width |
42	| `prefix + \|` | Split left/right (vertical divider) |
43	
44	\* `Ctrl + h/j/k/l` and `Ctrl + \` (vim-tmux-navigator) are gated on
45	the chezmoi `enableVimMode` prompt (default `true`). When `false`,
46	those bindings are omitted — `Ctrl+L` reaches the inner shell as
47	clear-screen, `Ctrl+H` as backspace, etc. Use `prefix + h/j/k/l` (kept
48	regardless) or `prefix + Arrow` for pane navigation. See
49	[`docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md`](../../this_repo/vim-mode.md).
50	| `prefix + -` | Split top/bottom (horizontal divider) |
51	| `prefix + c` | New window in current path |
52	| `prefix + x` | Kill pane (with confirmation) |
53	| `prefix + W` | Kill window (with confirmation) |
54	| `prefix + r` | Manually renumber windows (close index gaps) |
55	| `prefix + z` | Toggle pane zoom |
56	| `prefix + {` | Swap pane with previous (left/up) |
57	| `prefix + }` | Swap pane with next (right/down) |
58	| `prefix + m` | **Mark** current pane (built-in; one mark globally; needed by Join in menus) |
59	| `prefix + !` | Break current pane into a new window in same session (built-in) |
60	| `prefix + [` | Enter copy mode |
61	
62	`Ctrl+1..9` and `Ctrl+0` require CSI-u terminal support. Ghostty/cmux sends these natively. Alacritty needs explicit `keyboard.bindings` (managed by this repo in `dot_config/alacritty/alacritty.toml`). Legacy terminals (Terminal.app, plain SSH) cannot send these — use `prefix + number` instead.
63	
64	Swap-pane swaps the **content** while keeping the **sizes**. So if you have a 75%/25% split and swap, the left pane's content moves to the right (25%) and vice versa — the proportions stay fixed.
65	
66	## Layouts
67	
68	| Keybinding | Action |
69	|------------|--------|
70	| `M-1` | Even horizontal layout |
71	| `M-2` | Even vertical layout |
72	| `M-3` | Main horizontal layout |
73	| `M-4` | Main vertical layout |
74	| `M-5` | Tiled layout |
75	| `prefix + E` | Spread panes evenly (built-in) |
76	
77	`M-1` through `M-5` are tmux built-ins — no prefix needed; just hold Meta (Alt/Option) and press the number.
78	
79	> **macOS terminal requirement**: Option must send Meta/Esc+ for `M-` bindings to work. Ghostty/cmux: `macos-option-as-alt = left` (managed by this repo in `dot_config/ghostty/config`). Alacritty: `window.option_as_alt: OnlyLeft`. iTerm2: Profiles > Keys > Left Option Key > Esc+. See [docs/tools/ghostty.md](../ghostty.md).
80	
81	## Floating Pane (tmux-floax)
82	
83	| Keybinding | Action |
84	|------------|--------|
85	| `prefix + F` | Toggle floating pane (80% width/height, **persistent** `float` session) |
86	| `prefix + P` | Open floax popup menu |
87	| `prefix + \`` | One-shot **popup shell** at current pane path (each invocation = fresh shell, exits on `exit`/Ctrl-D) |
88	
89	Two flavours of popup shell, pick by use case:
90	
91	- **`prefix + \``** — quick-and-forget. Run a `curl`, check `df -h`, eyeball a file, exit. Each open is a clean shell. No history across opens. Good for "I just need to type one command without leaving my pane layout".
92	- **`prefix + F` (floax)** — scratchpad. The `float` session persists, so when you re-toggle the popup, your previous shell history, environment, and even running processes are still there. Good for "I'm iterating on something and don't want to lose the context".
93	
94	## One-shot Popups
95	
96	These open `display-popup -E` at `#{pane_current_path}`; the popup closes when the inner command exits. Unlike floax, no session persists.
97	
98	| Keybinding | Action |
99	|------------|--------|
100	| `prefix + G` | [`lazygit`](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit) popup |
101	| `prefix + T` | sesh picker (television) |
102	| `prefix + O` | sesh built-in picker |
103	| `prefix + U` | CLI tools picker (`tv tools`) |
104	| `prefix + u` | URL picker (tmux-fzf-url) |
105	| `prefix + a` | Live coding-agent panes picker (`tv agent-panes`) — see [agent pane discovery](../agent-panes-discovery.md) |
106	
107	When to use which:
108	
109	- **floax (`prefix + F`)** — repeated quick-access shell, want history preserved (notes, scratch math, long-running curl).
110	- **`prefix + \`` popup shell** — quick command in a fresh shell, exit and forget.
111	- **One-shot tool popup (`G`/...)** — start a TUI tool, do work, exit cleanly.
112	
113	## Help / Discovery (no more memorizing)
114	
115	The built-in `prefix + ?` (a wall-of-text `list-keys -N` dump) is replaced with [tmux-fzf](https://github.com/sainnhe/tmux-fzf): an fzf popup over **every** binding (including user-defined), fully fuzzy-searchable.
116	
117	| Keybinding | Action |
118	|------------|--------|
119	| `prefix + ?` | tmux-fzf: top-level fuzzy picker (keybindings / sessions / windows / panes / commands / processes / clipboard) |
120	| `prefix + C-?` | Plain `list-keys -N` (fallback if tmux-fzf is missing) |
121	| `prefix + /` | Built-in: prompt for a key, show what it's bound to (single-key lookup) |
122	| `prefix + Space` then `?` | Curated cheatsheet rendered with [`glow`](https://github.com/charmbracelet/glow) (source: `dot_config/tmux/cheatsheet.md`) |
123	| `prefix + Space` then `/` | tmux-fzf **keybinding** picker directly (skips the category menu) |
124	
125	Three layers of "I forgot the key" recovery:
126	
127	1. **Curated** (`prefix + Space`): grouped popup menu with the high-traffic top-level rows + submenus.
128	2. **Searchable** (`prefix + ?` → tmux-fzf): fuzzy-search across the full binding list.
129	3. **Reference** (`prefix + Space` → `?`): glow-rendered markdown cheatsheet (this file's `cheatsheet.md` sibling), good for browsing while learning.
130	
131	Why three? The popup menu is fastest once you know roughly what you want; tmux-fzf is for "I know it exists somewhere"; the cheatsheet is for "what's even possible?". Pick whichever matches your current uncertainty.
132	
133	## Copy Mode (Vim-Style)
134	
135	Enter with `prefix + [`. Navigate with vim keys, then:
136	
137	| Key | Action |
138	|-----|--------|
139	| `v` | Begin character selection (visual mode) |
140	| `V` | Select entire line |
141	| `C-v` | Toggle rectangle/block selection |
142	| `y` | Yank selection to system clipboard |
143	| `/` | Search forward |
144	| `?` | Search backward |
145	| `n`/`N` | Next/previous search match |
146	| `g`/`G` | Jump to top/bottom |
147	| `C-u`/`C-d` | Half-page up/down |
148	| `{` / `}` | Jump to previous / next prompt (needs OSC 133 — see [OSC 133](./README.md#osc-133-command-boundary-navigation-warp-style)) |
149	| `M-[` / `M-]` | Jump to previous / next command **output** start (needs OSC 133) |
150	| `q` or `Escape` | Exit copy mode |
151	
152	Mouse drag in copy mode also copies to clipboard. Double-click selects a word.
153	
154	Command-boundary keys (`{` `}` `M-[` `M-]`) rely on OSC 133 markers emitted by `dot_config/zsh/tools/02_shell_integration.zsh`. In a pane running a non-zsh shell or one that opted out via `DISABLE_OSC133=1`, they are silent no-ops.
155	
156	## Right-click menus
157	
158	Right-click opens a context menu depending on where you click:
159	
160	| Target | Menu items |
161	|--------|------------|
162	| Pane body (`MouseDown3Pane`) | Split h/v, swap up/down/left/right, zoom, resize 75% / even, mark, swap marked, **join marked here (h/v)**, **send pane to window…**, **break to new window**, copy mode, respawn, kill |
163	| Window list (`MouseDown3Status`) | Swap left/right, move/link to session, **merge into other window as pane (h/v)**, **even layout (horizontal / vertical / tiled)**, kill window, **renumber windows**, rename, new window |
164	| Session area on the left (`MouseDown3StatusLeft`) | Next/prev/choose/rename session, move current window, new session/window, kill session / kill-and-exit / kill-all-sessions |
165	
166	Our bindings use `display-menu -O` so the menu stays open after the mouse button is released — pick an item or press Escape to dismiss. (tmux's defaults omit `-O` and dismiss on release, which makes the menu unusable.)
167	
168	After break / send / merge / join, a status-bar message reports what happened (e.g. `Broke pane out to window 4 (zsh)`, `Merged into 1`).
169	
170	## URL Opening
171	
172	| Keybinding | Action |
173	|------------|--------|
174	| `prefix + u` | Open fzf popup listing all URLs in the pane (tmux-fzf-url) |
175	
176	In copy-mode (after selecting text with `v`):
177	
178	| Key | Action |
179	|-----|--------|
180	| `o` | Open selected URL/file in default browser/app (tmux-open) |
181	| `C-o` | Open selection in `$EDITOR` |
182	| `S` | Search selection in Google (tmux-open, configurable via `@open-S`) |
183	
184	Typical workflow: `prefix + u` for quick URL browsing; `prefix + [` then select + `o` for precise URL opening.
185	
186	## Capture Pane
187	
188	| Keybinding | Action |
189	|------------|--------|
190	| `prefix + y` | Copy visible pane content to system clipboard |
191	| `prefix + Y` | Copy full scrollback to system clipboard |
192	| `prefix + C-y` | Open scrollback in fzf, select lines to copy (Tab=multi) |
193	| `prefix + M-y` | Copy **last command's output** to clipboard (Warp-style, needs OSC 133 — see [OSC 133](./README.md#osc-133-command-boundary-navigation-warp-style)) |
194	| `prefix + M-i` | Copy **last command's input line** (prompt + typed command) to clipboard (needs OSC 133) |
195	
196	Cross-platform: `pbcopy` on macOS, `xclip`/`xsel` on Linux. OSC 52 also works for the vim-style `y` yank (even over SSH).
197	
198	## Moving Windows / Panes Across Sessions
199	
200	Like dragging a browser tab into a new window — but tmux can do it at three different granularities (whole window, pane → new window, pane → existing window as split). All cross-session/cross-window targets are picked from a `choose-tree` picker (live preview, fuzzy-search), not typed into a prompt. See the [picker-over-prompt design rule](#design-note-pickers-over-prompts) below for why.
201	
202	### Window-level (whole tab)
203	
204	| Key | Underlying command | Effect |
205	|-----|-------------------|--------|
206	| `prefix + M` | `choose-tree -Zs … move-window -s '#{window_id}' -t '%%'` | **Cut** current window out of this session and **paste** into target (session picker) |
207	| `prefix + A` | `choose-tree -Zs … link-window -s '#{window_id}' -t '%%:'` | **Link** (not copy): same window appears in both sessions; edits stay in sync. `unlink-window` removes one side without killing |
208	| `prefix + W` | `kill-window` | Kill current window (with confirmation) |
209	| `prefix + r` | `move-window -r` | Renumber windows in current session — closes index gaps. `renumber-windows on` (set in `common.conf`) auto-renumbers when a whole window is destroyed, but kill-pane on multi-pane windows or shell-driven exits can still leave gaps; this binding is the manual top-up. |
210	
211	### Pane → new window
212	
213	| Key | Underlying command | Effect |
214	|-----|-------------------|--------|
215	| `prefix + !` | `break-pane` (built-in) | Break current pane into a new window in the **same** session |
216	| `prefix + B` | `choose-tree -Zs … break-pane -s '#{pane_id}' -t '%%'` | Break + move to chosen session in one step (tab tear-out, session picker) |
217	| `prefix + E` | `~/.config/tmux/break-all-panes.sh` | **Explode** — break every pane in current window into its own window (same session). Source window keeps the first pane; others become sibling windows inserted right after, named after each pane's current command. Use case: continuing a wide-screen multi-pane layout on mobile/SSH where one pane per window is easier than zooming with `prefix + z`. Also available via right-click window menu → "Break all panes → windows". |
218	| Right-click pane → "Break to new window" | `break-pane` | Same as `prefix + !`, but reports the new window index in the status bar |
219	
220	### Pane → existing window (as a split)
221	
222	These all use tmux's `join-pane`, which moves a pane between windows. `join-pane` always operates on individual **panes**, not whole windows — there is no "merge two windows wholesale" command. The two-step "mark + join" idiom is the canonical workflow:
223	
224	1. Go to the **source** pane (the one you want to move).
225	2. Press `prefix + m` to **mark** it. tmux remembers exactly one marked pane globally; the marked pane gets a coloured border.
226	3. Switch to the **destination** window.
227	4. Right-click any pane → "Join marked pane here (h-split)" or "(v-split)". The marked pane jumps over and becomes a split.
228	
229	Alternative entry points to the same `join-pane` command:
230	
231	| From | Action | Effect |
232	|------|--------|--------|
233	| Right-click pane → "Join marked pane here (h/v-split)" | `join-pane -h` / `-v` | Pull the marked pane into this window as a split |
234	| Right-click pane → "Send pane to window…" | `choose-tree -Zw … join-pane -h -s '#{pane_id}' -t '%%'` | Push **this** pane out to another window as a split (no mark needed; pick target from window tree picker) |
235	| Right-click window tab → "Merge into other window (as pane, h/v-split)" | `choose-tree -Zw … join-pane -h -s '#{window_id}' -t '%%'` | Move this window's **active pane** into another window as a split. If the source window has only one pane, it disappears (effectively merging the whole window). With multiple panes, only the active one moves. |
236	| popup menu → Session → "Join marked here (h/v)" / "Send pane to…" | same as right-click | Same actions, keyboard-driven |
237	
238	> **Why no top-level `prefix +` key for join-pane / send-pane?** All single-letter capital slots are taken (`H/J/K/L` = resize, `S` = sesh-last, `W` = kill-window, `M/N/B/A` = window ops). Rather than rebind something else, these live in the right-click menus and the popup menu's Session submenu. The mark-and-join workflow is mostly mouse-friendly anyway.
239	
240	Tip: `prefix + s` (built-in choose-tree) shows live previews — handy for previewing sessions before invoking `M`/`B`/`A`, though those bindings now open their own pickers so the standalone preview is mostly for casual browsing.
241	
242	### Design note: pickers over prompts
243	
244	All cross-window/cross-session bindings in this repo use `choose-tree -Zw` (window picker) or `-Zs` (session picker), not `command-prompt`. Two reasons:
245	
246	1. **Correctness for `target-pane` commands**. tmux's `join-pane`, `swap-pane`, `move-pane` parse `-t TARGET` as a *pane* — a bare integer `N` means "pane index N in the *current* window", not "window N". Users typing `1` thinking "window 1" silently target the wrong pane (often the source pane itself, producing `Source and target panes must be different`). `choose-tree -Zw` returns `session:window`, which the parser unambiguously resolves to that window's active pane. Full debugging trail in [`pitfalls/tmux-join-pane-numeric-target-pane-not-window.md`](../../../pitfalls/tmux-join-pane-numeric-target-pane-not-window.md).
247	2. **UX**. Live preview, fuzzy-search, and zero memorisation of session names beat a free-form prompt even when both are technically safe (e.g. `move-window -t` accepts session-level targets without ambiguity).
248	
249	Source pane/window is always pinned with `-s '#{pane_id}'` or `-s '#{window_id}'` rather than relying on "current pane / current window" — `#{pane_id}` resolves at click time against the client's active pane, which may not be the right-clicked tab on status-bar menus.
250	
251	When adding a new keybinding/menu row that targets a window or session: reach for `choose-tree -Zw` / `-Zs` first; only fall back to `command-prompt` if no picker fits (free-form rename, brand-new session name, etc.).
252	
253	## Built-in tmux Keys Still Available
254	
255	| Keybinding | Action |
256	|------------|--------|
257	| `prefix + s` | Choose session tree |
258	| `prefix + w` | Choose window tree |
259	| `prefix + q` | Show pane numbers |
260	| `prefix + ,` | Rename window |
261	| `prefix + $` | Rename session |
262	| `prefix + ?` | tmux-fzf: fuzzy-search all keybindings (rebound from list-keys) |
263	| `prefix + C-?` | Built-in `list-keys -N` (fallback) |
264	| `prefix + /` | Prompt for a key and show what it is bound to |
265	
266	## Popup Menu (`prefix + Space`)
267	
268	The popup menu is bound to `prefix + Space` and is **generated by a script** (`~/.config/tmux/menu.sh`) rather than defined inline in `keybindings.conf`. Two reasons:
269	
270	1. **Quoting**. tmux's command parser stops at literal `;`, `{`, `}` even inside nested quotes. With ~50 menu rows full of fzf binds and shell one-liners, escaping in `keybindings.conf` was fragile and broke silently.
271	2. **Height-aware trimming**. `display-menu` does **not** paginate. If the menu is taller than the terminal, the entire popup is suppressed with no error. The script reads `#{client_height}` and emits one of three tier sets so the menu always fits.
272	
273	Tiers:
274	
275	| Terminal height | Top menu shows |
276	|-----------------|----------------|
277	| Any (Tier 0)    | Last window/pane, Choose win/sess, Pane #s, Sesh picker, Lazygit (~9 rows) |
278	| ≥ 14 (Tier 0+2) | + submenu launchers (`→ Layouts/Session/Sesh+/Popups/Theme/System`), Cheatsheet, Search keys |
279	| ≥ 22 (Tier 0+1+2) | + New window, Split `\|`/`-`, Zoom |
280	
281	Submenus are separate scripts (`menu-layouts.sh`, `menu-session.sh`, `menu-sesh.sh`, `menu-popups.sh`, `menu-theme.sh`, `menu-system.sh`), invoked from rows via `run-shell`. Each is an independent `display-menu` so quoting context resets.
282	
283	> **Historical note**: an earlier debugging round assumed `prefix + Space` and `prefix + Enter` were broken because of `extended-keys` / `csi-u` keysym encoding (tmux/tmux#4571, #4147, #4959, #4984), and the menu was moved to `prefix + e` as a workaround. That diagnosis was wrong. The actual failure was that the inline 50-row flat menu was **taller than the terminal**, and tmux silently suppresses oversized menus per `man tmux` ("If the menu is too large to fit on the terminal, it is not displayed."). Both `Space` and `Enter` were always bindable; the keysym story was a red herring. Full debugging trail in [`pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md`](../../../pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md). The menu was bound to both `Space` (canonical) and `e` (alias) for a while; the `e` alias has since been **removed** to free `e` as a sub-menu mnemonic (e.g. "Even layout: horizontal" in the window right-click menu). The canonical binding stays on `prefix + Space`.
284	
285	### Top-menu accelerator keys
286	
287	Accelerator keys match the standalone `prefix + key` bindings wherever possible — pressing `c` inside the menu does the same thing as `prefix + c` outside it.
288	
289	| Key | Row | Tier |
290	|-----|-----|------|
291	| `Tab` | Last window | 0 |
292	| `P` | Last pane | 0 |
293	| `w` | Choose window tree | 0 |
294	| `s` | Choose session tree | 0 |
295	| `q` | Show pane numbers | 0 |
296	| `g` | Sesh picker | 0 |
297	| `G` | Lazygit popup | 0 |
298	| `c` | New window | 1 (h ≥ 22) |
299	| `\|` | Split left/right | 1 |
300	| `-` | Split top/bottom | 1 |
301	| `z` | Zoom toggle | 1 |
302	| `L` | → Layouts submenu | 2 (h ≥ 14) |
303	| `S` | → Session submenu | 2 |
304	| `E` | → Sesh+ submenu | 2 |
305	| `o` | → Popups submenu | 2 |
306	| `T` | → Theme submenu | 2 |
307	| `Y` | → System submenu | 2 |
308	| `?` | Glow cheatsheet popup | 2 |
309	| `/` | tmux-fzf keybinding picker | 2 |
310	
311	### Submenu rows
312	
313	Source of truth: `dot_config/tmux/executable_menu-*.sh`.
314	
315	- **Layouts** (`L`): Even h/v (`1`/`2`), Main h/v (`3`/`4`), Tiled (`5`), Resize 75% (`+`), Pane h/j/k/l, Swap `{`/`}`.
316	- **Session** (`S`): Rename session/window (`$`/`,`), New session (`N`), Move window (`m`), Break pane (`r`), Link window (`K`), Renumber (`R`), Join marked here h/v (`j`/`J`), Send pane to (`s`), Kill pane/window/session/server (`x`/`W`/`X`/`Q`).
317	- **Sesh+** (`E`): TV picker (`V`), Built-in (`O`), Last sesh (`U`), scode here (`9`), CLI Tools tv (`B`).
318	- **Popups** (`o`): Lazygit (`g`), Shell (`s`), Floax scratchpad (`f`).
319	- **Theme** (`T`): Catppuccin (`c`), tmux2k (`t`).
320	- **System** (`Y`): Reload config (`R`), Install plugins (`I`), Update plugins (`U`), Detach (`d`), Clock (`k`).
321	
322	> **Hard cap**: the top menu is currently 14 rows at full height. Adding a 15th row will start failing on smaller terminals (mobile SSH, half-screen splits). Push lower-frequency items into a submenu instead, and re-test by shrinking the terminal vertically (heights 14 / 22 / 60).
323

28	        "Swap Down"  d { swap-pane -D } \
29	        "Swap Left"  l { swap-pane -t '{left-of}' } \
30	        "Swap Right" r { swap-pane -t '{right-of}' } \
31	        "" \
32	        "#{?window_zoomed_flag,Unzoom,Zoom}" z { resize-pane -Z } \
33	        "Resize 75%"  "+" { resize-pane -x 75% } \
34	        "Resize even"  "=" { select-layout even-horizontal } \
35	        "Mark pane"    m { select-pane -m } \
36	        "Swap marked"  s { swap-pane } \
37	        "Join marked pane here (h-split)" j { join-pane -h ; display-message "Joined marked pane here" } \
38	        "Join marked pane here (v-split)" J { join-pane -v ; display-message "Joined marked pane here" } \
39	        "Send pane to window... (h-split)" \
40	          S { choose-tree -Zw -F "#{window_name}" "join-pane -h -s '#{pane_id}' -t '%%' ; display-message 'Sent pane to target'" } \
41	        "Break to new window" \
42	          B { break-pane ; display-message "Broke pane out to window #{window_index} (#{window_name})" } \
43	        "" \
44	        "Enter copy mode" "[" { copy-mode } \
45	        "Respawn"     R { respawn-pane -k } \
46	        "Kill pane"   X { confirm-before -p "Kill pane? (y/n)" kill-pane } }
47	
48	unbind-key -n MouseDown3Status
49	# Window-tab right-click menu.
50	#
51	# WARNING: this menu is currently 23 visible rows, well above the ~14-row
52	# soft cap documented in AGENTS.md ("tmux ≥ 3.3 required for popup menu").
53	# tmux's display-menu silently suppresses itself if it can't fit on screen,
54	# so on small terminals (mobile SSH, half-height splits ~≤ 26 rows) the menu
55	# may not appear at all. Inlining (rather than nested submenus) is forced by
56	# pitfalls/tmux-submenu-flash-and-bottom-right.md — nested display-menu via
57	# run-shell from MouseDown3Status flashes / lands bottom-right / no-ops on
58	# second invocation. So everything stays flat here.
59	#
60	# The bottom block (⭐/📌/🔖/🚩 + Clear agent status) drives two per-window
61	# tmux user-options:
62	#   - @bookmark_status — manual tag, toggled by ~/.config/tmux/toggle-bookmark.sh
63	#   - @workmux_status  — agent state (🤖/💬/✅) written by workmux hooks; cleared
64	#                        here as the GUI equivalent of `wmclear` from 38_workmux.sh
65	# Both render side-by-side in the catppuccin window-text format (see
66	# theme.catppuccin.conf lines 31-32).
67	bind-key -n MouseDown3Status \
68	  display-menu -O -T "#[align=centre]#{window_index}:#{window_name}" -t = -x W -y W \
69	    "Swap Left"  l { swap-window -t :-1 } \
70	    "Swap Right" r { swap-window -t :+1 } \
71	    "" \
72	    "Even horizontal" 1 { select-layout even-horizontal } \
73	    "Even vertical"   2 { select-layout even-vertical } \
74	    "Main horizontal" 3 { select-layout main-horizontal } \
75	    "Main vertical"   4 { select-layout main-vertical } \
76	    "Tiled (grid)"    5 { select-layout tiled } \
77	    "" \
78	    "Move to session..." m { choose-tree -Zs -F "#{session_name}" "move-window -s '#{window_id}' -t '%%'" } \
79	    "Link to session..." K { choose-tree -Zs -F "#{session_name}" "link-window -s '#{window_id}' -t '%%:'" } \
80	    "Break all panes → windows" E { run-shell "~/.config/tmux/break-all-panes.sh" } \
81	    "" \
82	    "Kill window" X { kill-window } \
83	    "Renumber windows" N { move-window -r ; display-message "Windows renumbered" } \
84	    "Rename"      n { command-prompt -F -I "#W" { rename-window -t "#{window_id}" "%%" } } \
85	    "" \
86	    "⭐ Star"     s { run-shell "~/.config/tmux/toggle-bookmark.sh '#{window_id}' '⭐'" } \
87	    "📌 Pin"      p { run-shell "~/.config/tmux/toggle-bookmark.sh '#{window_id}' '📌'" } \
88	    "🔖 Bookmark" b { run-shell "~/.config/tmux/toggle-bookmark.sh '#{window_id}' '🔖'" } \
89	    "🚩 Flag"     f { run-shell "~/.config/tmux/toggle-bookmark.sh '#{window_id}' '🚩'" } \
90	    "Clear agent status" c { set-option -w -t "#{window_id}" -u "@workmux_status" ; display-message "Cleared @workmux_status on #{window_index}:#{window_name}" } \
91	    "" \
92	    "New window"  w { new-window }
93	
94	unbind-key -n MouseDown3StatusLeft
95	bind-key -n MouseDown3StatusLeft \
96	  display-menu -O -T "#[align=centre]#{session_name}" -t = -x M -y W \
97	    Next        n { switch-client -n } \
98	    Previous    p { switch-client -p } \
99	    "" \
100	    "Choose session..." c { choose-tree -Zs } \
101	    Rename      N { command-prompt -I "#S" { rename-session "%%" } } \
102	    "" \
103	    "Move current window to..." m { choose-tree -Zs -F "#{session_name}" "move-window -s '#{window_id}' -t '%%'" } \
104	    "" \
105	    "New session" s { new-session } \
106	    "New window"  w { new-window } \
107	    "" \
108	    "Kill session"        X { kill-session } \
109	    "Kill session & exit" E { run-shell "~/.config/tmux/kill-session-exit.sh" } \
110	    "Kill all sessions"   Q { confirm-before -p "Kill ALL sessions (tmux server)? (y/n)" kill-server }
