112	# =============================================================================
113	# Vim-Style Copy Mode (prefix + [ to enter, q to exit)
114	# =============================================================================
115	#
116	#   h/j/k/l  move cursor        C-u/C-d  half-page up/down
117	#   g/G      top/bottom          //?      search forward/backward
118	#   v        begin selection     V        line selection
119	#   C-v      rectangle select    y        yank to clipboard
120	#   Escape   clear selection     q        exit copy mode
121	
122	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} v send-keys -X begin-selection
123	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} V send-keys -X select-line
124	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} C-v send-keys -X rectangle-toggle
125	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} y send-keys -X copy-selection-and-cancel
126	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} MouseDragEnd1Pane send-keys -X copy-selection
127	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} DoubleClick1Pane select-pane \; send-keys -X select-word
128	
129	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
130	# Command-boundary navigation in copy-mode (Warp-style).
131	# Requires OSC 133 markers from the shell — emitted by
132	# dot_config/zsh/tools/02_shell_integration.zsh. In a plain shell (no markers,
133	# e.g. `sh`, `bash` without our hook, or `DISABLE_OSC133=1`), these keys are
134	# no-ops. tmux 3.4+ required for next-prompt/previous-prompt; the `-o` variant
135	# (jump to output start, not prompt start) is tmux 3.5+.
136	#
137	#   {  / }    previous/next prompt (the prompt line itself)
138	#   M-[ / M-] previous/next command output (line AFTER the prompt — usually
139	#             what you want for "skip to the output of the previous command")
140	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
141	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} '{' send-keys -X previous-prompt
142	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} '}' send-keys -X next-prompt
143	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} M-[ send-keys -X previous-prompt -o
144	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} M-] send-keys -X next-prompt -o
145	
146	# =============================================================================
147	# Capture Pane Helpers
148	# =============================================================================
149	
150	# prefix + y: copy visible pane content to system clipboard
151	# `load-buffer -w -` loads into tmux's paste buffer AND forwards to the outer
152	# terminal via OSC 52 (requires `set-clipboard on` in common.conf). This works
153	# over SSH without shelling out to pbcopy/xclip on the remote host.
154	bind y run-shell "tmux capture-pane -p | tmux load-buffer -w - && tmux display-message 'Pane content copied to clipboard'"
155	
156	# prefix + Y: copy full scrollback to system clipboard
157	bind Y run-shell "tmux capture-pane -pS - | tmux load-buffer -w - && tmux display-message 'Full scrollback copied to clipboard'"
158	
159	# prefix + C-y: capture pane into fzf for line-by-line selection, yank chosen lines
160	bind C-y run-shell "\
161	  tmux capture-pane -pS - | fzf-tmux -p 80%,70% --multi --tac --no-sort \
162	    --header 'Select lines to copy (Tab=multi, Enter=copy)' \
163	    | tmux load-buffer -w - && tmux display-message 'Selected lines copied'"
164	
165	# prefix + M-y: copy the LAST command's OUTPUT to clipboard (Warp-style).
166	# Requires OSC 133 markers — if the shell doesn't emit them (non-zsh shell,
167	# DISABLE_OSC133=1, or a remote bash without our hook), selection ends up
168	# empty. Chain: enter copy-mode, jump to start of previous command's output,
169	# begin selection, jump forward to the next prompt (end of output), copy,
170	# flash confirmation.
171	bind M-y copy-mode \; \
172	  send-keys -X previous-prompt -o \; \
173	  send-keys -X begin-selection \; \
174	  send-keys -X next-prompt \; \
175	  send-keys -X copy-pipe-and-cancel "tmux load-buffer -w -" \; \
176	  display-message "Last command output copied to clipboard"
177	
178	# prefix + M-i: copy the LAST command's INPUT LINE (prompt + typed command).
179	# Same dependency on OSC 133 markers. Because we don't emit the B marker
180	# (end-of-prompt), the copied text includes prompt chrome (e.g. "❯ echo hi"
181	# not just "echo hi"). Trim in the paste target if needed. Chain: enter
182	# copy-mode, jump to the previous prompt's A marker, begin selection, jump
183	# forward to the C marker (= start of output = end of input line), copy.
184	bind M-i copy-mode \; \
185	  send-keys -X previous-prompt \; \
186	  send-keys -X begin-selection \; \
187	  send-keys -X next-prompt -o \; \
188	  send-keys -X copy-pipe-and-cancel "tmux load-buffer -w -" \; \
189	  display-message "Last command input (prompt+line) copied to clipboard"
190	
191	# =============================================================================
192	# Vim-Style Pane Navigation
193	# =============================================================================
194	
195	bind h select-pane -L
196	bind j select-pane -D
197	bind k select-pane -U
198	bind l select-pane -R
199	
200	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
201	# vim-tmux-navigator: prefix-less Ctrl+h/j/k/l crosses tmux panes <-> vim splits
202	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
203	# Detect if the current pane is running vim/neovim; if so forward the key,
204	# otherwise move between tmux panes. Matches christoomey/vim-tmux-navigator.
205	# Gated on chezmoi `enableVimMode` (default true). When off, Ctrl+h/j/k/l
206	# pass through to the inner shell (Ctrl+L = clear, Ctrl+H = backspace, etc.).
207	# See docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md.
208	{{ if .enableVimMode -}}
209	is_vim="ps -o state= -o comm= -t '#{pane_tty}' | grep -iqE '^[^TXZ ]+ +(\\S+\\/)?g?\\.?(view|n?vim?x?)(-wrapped)?(diff)?$'"
210	bind-key -n 'C-h' if-shell "$is_vim" 'send-keys C-h'  'select-pane -L'
211	bind-key -n 'C-j' if-shell "$is_vim" 'send-keys C-j'  'select-pane -D'
212	bind-key -n 'C-k' if-shell "$is_vim" 'send-keys C-k'  'select-pane -U'
213	bind-key -n 'C-l' if-shell "$is_vim" 'send-keys C-l'  'select-pane -R'
214	# NOTE: C-\ (select-pane -l) removed — tmux 3.4+ cannot parse C-\ in config files.
215	# Use directional C-h/j/k/l instead, or prefix+; for last-pane.
216	
217	bind-key -T copy-mode-vi 'C-h' select-pane -L
218	bind-key -T copy-mode-vi 'C-j' select-pane -D
219	bind-key -T copy-mode-vi 'C-k' select-pane -U
220	bind-key -T copy-mode-vi 'C-l' select-pane -R
221	{{- else -}}
222	# enableVimMode = false: vim-tmux-navigator omitted. Use prefix + h/j/k/l
223	# (kept below) or prefix + Arrow for pane navigation.
224	{{- end }}
225	
226	# Intuitive split bindings (| = left/right, - = top/bottom)
227	bind | split-window -h -c "#{pane_current_path}"
228	bind - split-window -v -c "#{pane_current_path}"
229	
230	# Resize panes with prefix + H/J/K/L (5 cells)
231	bind -r H resize-pane -L 5
232	bind -r J resize-pane -D 5
233	bind -r K resize-pane -U 5
234	bind -r L resize-pane -R 5
235	
236	# Fine resize with Meta + h/j/k/l (1 cell, repeatable)
237	bind -r M-h resize-pane -L 1
238	bind -r M-j resize-pane -D 1
239	bind -r M-k resize-pane -U 1
240	bind -r M-l resize-pane -R 1
241	
242	# Quick ratio: set current pane to 75% width
243	bind + resize-pane -x 75%
244	
245	# =============================================================================
246	# Quick Window Switching (Ctrl+Number, requires CSI-u / extended-keys)
247	# =============================================================================
248	# Supplement to prefix + 1..9 (tmux built-in defaults, always available).
249	# These require extended-keys (CSI-u) support from the terminal emulator
250	# (Ghostty/cmux, Alacritty, Kitty, WezTerm). Legacy terminals (Terminal.app,
251	# plain SSH) will not send these sequences — use prefix + number instead.
252	# Note: prefix + 9 / prefix + 0 are rebound below (scode / sesh-root for
253	# current dir), so Ctrl+9 below is the only way to reach window 9 from
254	# the keyboard. Ctrl+0 mirrors prefix+0 (lightweight sesh-root) since
255	# base-index is 1 and window 0 doesn't exist.
256	
257	bind-key -n C-1 select-window -t :=1
258	bind-key -n C-2 select-window -t :=2
259	bind-key -n C-3 select-window -t :=3
260	bind-key -n C-4 select-window -t :=4
261	bind-key -n C-5 select-window -t :=5
262	bind-key -n C-6 select-window -t :=6
263	bind-key -n C-7 select-window -t :=7
264	bind-key -n C-8 select-window -t :=8
265	bind-key -n C-9 select-window -t :=9
266	bind-key -n C-0 run-shell -b "~/.config/tmux/sesh-root-here.sh '#{pane_current_path}'"
267	
268	# New window/pane inherits current path
269	bind c new-window -c "#{pane_current_path}"
270	
271	# Reload config with prefix + R
272	bind R source-file "$HOME/.tmux.conf" \; display-message "Sourced ~/.tmux.conf"
273	
274	# Session management
275	bind N command-prompt -p "New session:" "new-session -s '%%'"
276	bind X confirm-before -p "Kill session #S? (y/n)" kill-session
277	# Kill current session AND detach client (return to parent shell).
278	# Differs from `prefix + X` above, which keeps you inside tmux by
279	# switching to another session (detach-on-destroy off, common.conf).
280	# Chained via helper script because `confirm-before` takes a single
281	# tmux command; inline `\;` inside its string arg is not parsed as a
282	# command separator.
283	bind M-x confirm-before -p "Kill session #S and exit tmux? (y/n)" \
284	  "run-shell '$HOME/.config/tmux/kill-session-exit.sh'"
285	bind x confirm-before -p "Kill pane? (y/n)" kill-pane
286	bind W confirm-before -p "Kill window #W? (y/n)" kill-window
287	
288	# Manual renumber (renumber-windows on usually handles this, but kill-pane on
289	# multi-pane windows or shell-driven exits can leave gaps).
290	bind r move-window -r \; display-message "Windows renumbered"
291	
292	# =============================================================================
293	# Move/Break Windows Across Sessions (GUI tab tear-out feel)
294	# =============================================================================
295	# prefix + M : move current window to another session (interactive prompt).
296	#              Target form: "session:" (auto-pick index) or "session:index"
297	#              (use -k via "!session:index" trick? simpler: bare prompt).
298	#              Tab-completes existing sessions.
299	# prefix + B : break current pane into a new window AND move it to a target
300	#              session in one go (acts like dragging a tab out).
301	# prefix + A : link current window into another session (window appears in
302	#              both sessions; edit either, both update). Use prefix + & to
303	#              kill, or unlink-window to detach without killing.
304	#
305	# Cross-window pane operations (no top-level prefix binding — letter slots are
306	# saturated by resize-pane H/J/K/L and sesh-last S; pane join/send live in the
307	# right-click pane menu and the popup menu's Session submenu instead):
308	#   - Mark current pane:  prefix + m  (built-in)
309	#   - Pull marked pane:   right-click pane menu → "Join marked pane here"
310	#   - Push current pane:  right-click pane menu → "Send pane to..."
311	#   - Break out to new window: right-click pane menu → "Break to new window"
312	#                              or prefix + ! (built-in, same session)
313	#                              or prefix + B (break + move to chosen session)
314	
315	bind M run-shell "tmux set-environment -g _src_window '#{window_id}'" \; \
316	  display-message "Pick destination session to MOVE window into…" \; \
317	  choose-tree -Zs -F "#{session_name}" \
318	  "run-shell '~/.config/tmux/cross-session.sh move %%'"
319	bind B run-shell "tmux set-environment -g _src_pane '#{pane_id}'" \; \
320	  display-message "Pick destination session to BREAK pane into (as new window)…" \; \
321	  choose-tree -Zs -F "#{session_name}" \
322	  "run-shell '~/.config/tmux/cross-session.sh break %%'"
323	bind A run-shell "tmux set-environment -g _src_window '#{window_id}'" \; \
324	  display-message "Pick destination session to LINK window into (window lives in both)…" \; \
325	  choose-tree -Zs -F "#{session_name}" \
326	  "run-shell '~/.config/tmux/cross-session.sh link %%'"
327	
328	# prefix + E : explode — break EVERY pane in current window into its own window
329	#              within the SAME session. Use case: switching from wide screen
330	#              (multi-pane layout) to mobile/SSH where one pane per window is
331	#              easier than zooming with prefix + z. Source window keeps the
332	#              first pane; other panes become sibling windows inserted right
333	#              after it, named after each pane's current command.
334	bind E run-shell "~/.config/tmux/break-all-panes.sh"
335	
336	# =============================================================================
337	# Theme Switching (Catppuccin <-> tmux2k)
338	# =============================================================================
339	# Note: first-time switch requires `prefix + I` to install the target plugin.
340	
341	bind M-c run-shell "tmux set -g @theme_variant catppuccin; \
342	  tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf; \
343	  tmux display-message 'Theme: catppuccin'"
344	
345	bind M-t run-shell "tmux set -g @theme_variant tmux2k; \
346	  tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf; \
347	  tmux display-message 'Theme: tmux2k'"
348	
349	# =============================================================================
350	# Sesh (tmux session manager)
351	# =============================================================================
352	
353	# prefix + g: sesh picker in a tmux popup with fzf
354	bind-key "g" run-shell "sesh connect \"$(\
355	  sesh list --icons | fzf-tmux -p 80%,70% \
356	    --no-sort --ansi --border-label ' sesh ' --prompt '⚡  ' \
357	    --header '  ^a all ^t tmux ^g configs ^x zoxide ^d tmux kill ^f find' \
358	    --bind 'tab:down,btab:up' \
359	    --bind 'ctrl-a:change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
360	    --bind 'ctrl-t:change-prompt(🪟  )+reload(sesh list -t --icons)' \
361	    --bind 'ctrl-g:change-prompt(⚙️  )+reload(sesh list -c --icons)' \
362	    --bind 'ctrl-x:change-prompt(📁  )+reload(sesh list -z --icons)' \
363	    --bind 'ctrl-f:change-prompt(🔎  )+reload(fd -H -d 2 -t d -E .Trash . ~)' \
364	    --bind 'ctrl-d:execute(tmux kill-session -t {2..})+change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
365	    --preview-window 'right:55%' \
366	    --preview 'sesh preview {}' \
367	)\""
368	
369	bind -N "last-session (via sesh)" S run-shell "sesh last 2>/dev/null || tmux display-message 'No previous sesh session'"
370	
371	# prefix + 9: open repo-aware coding-agent layout (`scode`) for the current
372	# pane's directory. scode walks up from cwd to find .git; if not in a repo,
373	# the error surfaces in the tmux status line.
374	# Replaces the previous `sesh connect --root $(pwd)` binding (which had a
375	# subtle bug — $(pwd) was expanded once at config parse time, not per-press).
376	# Logic is in scode-here.sh because tmux run-shell is /bin/sh (can't see
377	# zsh functions) and the session-name + switch-client dance is non-trivial.
378	bind -N "scode for current dir (repo-aware coding layout)" 9 \
379	  run-shell -b "~/.config/tmux/scode-here.sh '#{pane_current_path}'"
380	
381	# prefix + 0: lightweight counterpart to prefix+9. Plain sesh session at
382	# the git root of the current pane's directory (no nvim/agent layout).
383	# Replaces tmux's built-in `select-window -t :=0` which always errored
384	# because base-index is 1 (no window 0 exists). Logic in sesh-root-here.sh
385	# — see that file for the two bugs in the original `sesh connect --root
386	# $(pwd)` binding (parse-time $(pwd) + misuse of --root flag).
387	bind -N "sesh-root for current dir (lightweight)" 0 \
388	  run-shell -b "~/.config/tmux/sesh-root-here.sh '#{pane_current_path}'"
389	
390	# prefix + T: sesh picker via television (tv) in a tmux popup
391	bind-key "T" display-popup -E -w 80% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' Sesh (tv) ' "tv sesh"
392	
393	# prefix + O: sesh built-in picker in a tmux popup
394	bind-key "O" display-popup -h 90% -w 50% -E "sesh picker -i"
395	
396	# prefix + U: CLI tools picker via television (tv tools)
397	bind-key "U" display-popup -E -w 80% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' CLI Tools (tv) ' "tv tools"
398	
399	# prefix + a: live coding-agent panes picker (tv agent-panes)
400	# Shows claude / cursor-agent / codex / opencode sessions currently running in
401	# any tmux pane. Enter switches focus to that pane. See:
402	#   docs/tools/agent-panes-discovery.md
403	bind-key "a" display-popup -E -w 80% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' Live agent panes (tv) ' "tv agent-panes"
404	
405	# (prefix + W is now bound earlier in this file as `kill-window`. The previous
406	# `sesh window` binding was removed because `sesh` has no `window` subcommand;
407	# pressing it printed sesh's help to a popup. See git history.)
408	
409	# =============================================================================
410	# Popup tools (display-popup -E -d '#{pane_current_path}')
411	# =============================================================================
412	# Floating scratch pane (tmux-floax) is on prefix + F (toggleable, persistent
413	# session named `float`). The bindings below are one-shot popups that close
414	# when the inner command exits — handy for "do one thing without disrupting
415	# the layout" workflows.
416	
417	# prefix + G: lazygit popup at current pane path
418	bind-key "G" display-popup -E -w 90% -h 90% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' lazygit ' "lazygit"
419	
420	# prefix + ` (backtick): one-shot popup shell at current pane path.
421	# Closes when the inner shell exits (`exit` or Ctrl-D). Each invocation gets
422	# a fresh shell — no state preserved. For a persistent scratchpad with
423	# history, use floax (prefix + F) instead.
424	bind-key '`' display-popup -E -w 80% -h 80% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' shell '
425	
426	# =============================================================================
427	# Help / cheatsheet
428	# =============================================================================
429	# tmux's built-in `prefix + ?` (list-keys -N) is hard to scan and can't search
430	# user-defined bindings well. We replace it with tmux-fzf's keybinding picker
431	# (fzf popup, fuzzy-searchable). The original list-keys is still reachable on
432	# `prefix + C-?` as a fallback.
433	#
434	# `prefix + /` (built-in: prompt for a key, show what it's bound to) is left
435	# alone — it's already useful for "what does THIS key do?" lookups.
436	#
437	# `?` inside the prefix + Enter popup menu opens a glow-rendered
438	# cheatsheet (curated, grouped, prettier than list-keys).
439	
440	unbind-key '?'
441	bind-key '?' run-shell -b "~/.tmux/plugins/tmux-fzf/main.sh"
442	bind-key 'C-?' list-keys -N
443	
444	# `/` inside the Enter-popup uses this; standalone prefix + / stays built-in
445	# (key-prompt). We expose the cheatsheet through the popup menu's `?` entry.
446	bind-key M-/ display-popup -E -w 80% -h 80% -T ' tmux cheatsheet ' \
447	  "glow -p ~/.config/tmux/cheatsheet.md 2>/dev/null \
448	    || less ~/.config/tmux/cheatsheet.md"
449	
450	# =============================================================================
451	# Popup Menu (prefix + Space)
452	# =============================================================================
453	# Two entry keys, same menu. The menu itself is generated by a script
454	# (`~/.config/tmux/menu.sh`) which:
455	#
456	#   1. Reads `#{client_height}` and emits a tier-trimmed row list. tmux's
457	#      `display-menu` does NOT paginate — if the menu is taller than the
458	#      terminal, the entire popup is silently suppressed (no error). The
459	#      script keeps the menu fitting on tiny mobile-SSH heights too.
460	#   2. Submenus are sibling scripts (menu-layouts.sh, menu-session.sh,
461	#      menu-sesh.sh, menu-popups.sh, menu-theme.sh, menu-system.sh). Each
462	#      `exec tmux display-menu …` so quoting context resets per submenu —
463	#      no nested-quote escaping disasters in keybindings.conf.
464	#
465	# History: an earlier flat ~50-row menu silently failed on smaller heights
466	# and was misdiagnosed as a csi-u key encoding bug, then as a quoting bug.
467	# Both real (the `\;` accelerator was broken, sesh fzf binds had nested-
468	# quote issues), but the dominant symptom — "menu doesn't open at all" —
469	# was actually menu-too-tall. See pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-parse-failure.md.
470	#
471	# Discovery fallbacks if you forget the keys: `prefix + ?` (tmux-fzf fuzzy
472	# picker over every binding), `prefix + M-/` (glow cheatsheet popup), or
473	# right-click on a pane / status line.
474	
475	unbind-key Space
476	unbind-key Enter
477	bind-key Space run-shell "~/.config/tmux/menu.sh"
478	# Note: `prefix + e` was previously a popup-menu alias (added as workaround
479	# for a misdiagnosed display-menu bug — see pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md).
480	# Removed so `e` is free as a sub-menu mnemonic (e.g. "Even layout: horizontal"
481	# in the window right-click menu).
482

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Detach all clients of the current tmux session, then destroy the session.
3	# Gives "kill current session and return to parent shell" behavior even
4	# when `detach-on-destroy off` is set globally (common.conf), which would
5	# otherwise make `kill-session` switch to another session instead.
6	set -euo pipefail
7	
8	session=$(tmux display-message -p '#S')
9	tmux detach-client -s "$session"
10	tmux kill-session -t "$session"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Top-level tmux popup menu — invoked by `prefix + Space`.
3	#
4	# Why a script (not inline `display-menu` in keybindings.conf):
5	#   1. tmux's command parser stops at literal `;`, `{`, `}` even inside
6	#      nested quotes. With ~50 menu rows full of fzf binds and shell
7	#      one-liners, escaping became fragile and broke silently.
8	#   2. tmux `display-menu` does not paginate. If the menu is taller than
9	#      the terminal, the entire popup is suppressed with no error. By
10	#      generating the menu here we can read $TMUX client_height and
11	#      auto-trim low-frequency rows when small.
12	#   3. Submenus are normal `tmux display-menu` invocations from rows;
13	#      they don't share quoting context with the parent menu.
14	#
15	# Submenus live in sibling scripts:
16	#   menu-layouts.sh, menu-session.sh, menu-sesh.sh,
17	#   menu-popups.sh, menu-theme.sh, menu-system.sh, menu-agents.sh
18	#
19	# See: pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-parse-failure.md
20	
21	set -euo pipefail
22	
23	H=$(tmux display-message -p '#{client_height}')
24	DIR=~/.config/tmux
25	
26	# Tier 0: ALWAYS shown (highest frequency, ~7 rows + 2 separators)
27	declare -a tier0=(
28	  "Last window"  Tab "last-window"
29	  "Last pane"    P   "last-pane"
30	  ""             ""  ""
31	  "Choose win"   w   "choose-tree -Zw"
32	  "Choose sess"  s   "choose-tree -Zs"
33	  "Pane #s"      q   "display-panes -d 0"
34	  ""             ""  ""
35	  "Sesh picker"  g   "run-shell '$DIR/sesh-picker.sh'"
36	  "Lazygit"      G   "display-popup -E -w 90% -h 90% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' lazygit ' 'lazygit'"
37	)
38	
39	# Tier 1: shown when height >= 22 (adds new-window/split/zoom)
40	declare -a tier1=(
41	  ""             ""  ""
42	  "New window"   c   "new-window -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
43	  "Split |"      "|" "split-window -h -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
44	  "Split -"      "-" "split-window -v -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
45	  "Zoom"         z   "resize-pane -Z"
46	)
47	
48	# Tier 2: submenus + cheatsheet (always shown if Tier 1 is shown)
49	declare -a tier2=(
50	  ""             ""  ""
51	  "→ Layouts"    L   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-layouts.sh'"
52	  "→ Session"    S   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-session.sh'"
53	  "→ Sesh+"      E   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-sesh.sh'"
54	  "→ Agents"     A   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-agents.sh'"
55	  "→ Popups"     o   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-popups.sh'"
56	  "→ Theme"      T   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-theme.sh'"
57	  "→ System"     Y   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-system.sh'"
58	  ""             ""  ""
59	  "Cheatsheet"   "?" "display-popup -E -w 80% -h 80% -T ' tmux cheatsheet ' 'glow -p $DIR/cheatsheet.md 2>/dev/null || less $DIR/cheatsheet.md'"
60	  "Search keys"  "/" "run-shell -b ~/.tmux/plugins/tmux-fzf/scripts/keybinding.sh"
61	)
62	
63	rows=("${tier0[@]}")
64	if [ "$H" -ge 22 ]; then
65	  rows+=("${tier1[@]}" "${tier2[@]}")
66	elif [ "$H" -ge 14 ]; then
67	  rows+=("${tier2[@]}")
68	fi
69	
70	exec tmux display-menu -T "#[align=centre,bold]tmux (h=$H)" -x R -y P "${rows[@]}"
71
```

41	### Workmux status icon integration spans 6 files
42	
43	Touching the `🤖`/`💬`/`✅` per-tmux-window status mechanism requires keeping these 6 surfaces in sync (full story: [docs/tools/workmux.md](docs/tools/workmux.md); pitfall: [pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md](pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md)):
44	
45	1. `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` — binary install (brew tap on macOS; GitHub release `.tar.gz` on Linux)
46	2. `dot_config/workmux/config.yaml` — `status_format: false` is load-bearing
47	3. `dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf` — `#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}` appended to `@catppuccin_window_text` and `@catppuccin_window_current_text`
48	4. `dot_claude/modify_settings.json` — `Stop`/`SubagentStop`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`Notification` hooks calling `workmux set-window-status` (hook-aware merger preserves CodeIsland entries)
49	5. `dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts` + `dot_config/opencode/modify_package.json`
50	6. `dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh` — generic POSIX `tmux_status_set/get/clear/clear_all/list/run` for non-agent producers
51	
52	**Hard rules**: never run `workmux setup` on a managed machine (would write parallel hook entries); never flip `status_format: true` (fights catppuccin's window-text override); never drop the `command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && … || true` guard in Claude hooks (spams errors on fresh boxes); never drop explicit `set-window-status done` from `Stop`/`SubagentStop` (upstream only ever sets `working`, never clears — that's the by-design leak documented in the pitfall). `wt` (worktrunk, `37_worktrunk.zsh`) and `wm` (workmux, `38_workmux.zsh`) stay distinct — different config formats, killer features, helper files.

64	
65	## Chezmoi templating conventions
66	
67	**Hard rule**: before adding `{{ if eq .profile … }}`, ask if the predicate is auto-detectable. If yes, use `.chezmoi.os` / `.chezmoi.arch` / `.chezmoi.hostname`. `.profile` is for user-role choices only. Values are limited to `macos`, `ubuntu_desktop`, `ubuntu_server` — do **not** introduce new values for OS/arch facts (historical `macos_intel` profile was removed for exactly this reason).
68	
69	| Predicate | Use |
70	|---|---|
71	| Any macOS | `eq .chezmoi.os "darwin"` |
72	| Any Linux | `eq .chezmoi.os "linux"` |
73	| Apple Silicon | `eq .chezmoi.arch "arm64"` (in darwin scope) or `and (eq .chezmoi.os "darwin") (eq .chezmoi.arch "arm64")` |
74	| Intel Mac | `and (eq .chezmoi.os "darwin") (eq .chezmoi.arch "amd64")` |
75	| Desktop vs headless | `.profile` — `ubuntu_desktop` / `ubuntu_server` |
76	
77	Decision table, before/after examples, `macos_intel` migration: [docs/tools/chezmoi-templating.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-templating.md).
78	
79	## Hard repo invariants
80	
81	### Validate app configs with the app, not just syntax
82	
83	Template rendering / YAML / TOML / JSON syntax is not enough. If the app exposes a config check, parser, dry-run, or debug command, run it against the rendered config before declaring done (e.g. `codex debug …` for `~/.codex/config.toml`; `tmux source-file` / `display-menu` smoke for tmux; `mkdocs build --strict` for docs; for Ansible run the narrowest practical play/tag/check-mode or container smoke — `--syntax-check` alone is a first pass). If a validator cannot be run, say so explicitly in the final report and name the missing command/host/credential.
84	
85	### `primaryShell` choice gates `chsh` only — both shells always deploy
86	
87	`primaryShell` (`zsh` | `bash`, default `zsh`) **only** governs which login shell `chsh` switches to. Both `~/.zshrc`, `~/.bashrc`, `~/.config/{shell,zsh,bash}/` deploy everywhere — users routinely drop into the other shell ad-hoc.
88	
89	**Hard rules**:
90	
91	- Do **not** add `{{ if eq .primaryShell … }}` gates around `dot_zshrc.tmpl`, `dot_bashrc.tmpl`, or `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/**`.
92	- Do **not** gate the zsh / bash ansible roles' **package install** task on `primary_shell` — only `chsh` is gated. macOS bash 5.x brew install + `/etc/shells` whitelist are gated on `primary_shell == "bash"` (zsh-primary mac users skip the brew formula).
93	- Do **not** rely on `$SHELL` — it reflects `/etc/passwd`, lags `chsh` until next login. Use `$ZSH_VERSION` / `$BASH_VERSION`.
94	
95	ble.sh + oh-my-bash 12-step init order in `dot_bashrc.tmpl` is load-bearing: `ble.sh --attach=none` MUST source before bash-preexec/starship; `ble-attach` MUST be the last call before secrets/adhoc; OMB's `autosuggestions` / `syntax-highlighting` / `history-substring-search` plugins MUST be excluded (ble.sh provides natives; double-init causes flicker). Full breakdown: [docs/shells/bash.md](docs/shells/bash.md).
96	
97	### Three-tier user-local override layer
98	
99	User overrides live in **six** untracked files: shared POSIX (`~/.shellrc.adhoc`, `~/.shellrc.secrets`) and per-shell (`~/.zshrc.adhoc`, `~/.bashrc.adhoc`, `~/.config/zsh/secrets.zsh`, `~/.config/bash/secrets.sh`). All six in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`. Default target: shared. Drop to per-shell only when shell-specific syntax is required.
100	
101	**Load order** in both `dot_zshrc.tmpl` and `dot_bashrc.tmpl`:
102	
103	```
104	managed modules → shared secrets → per-shell secrets → shared adhoc → per-shell adhoc
105	```
106	
107	Secrets before adhoc (so adhoc can read secret vars); shared before per-shell (per-shell wins on conflict).
108	
109	**Hard rules**: never add the shared files to chezmoi management; never auto-stub the `*.secrets` files (empty secrets footgun); the shared adhoc stub heredoc lives in BOTH `dot_zshrc.tmpl` AND `dot_bashrc.tmpl` (first shell to run wins; second sees the file and skips) — keep both heredoc bodies in sync. Full matrix: [docs/shells/adhoc-and-secrets.md](docs/shells/adhoc-and-secrets.md).
110	
111	### `enableVimMode` gates shell + tmux vim, NOT Neovim or editors
112	
113	`enableVimMode` (bool, default `true`) gates **shell modal editing + tmux vim navigation only**. Neovim and every editor config (VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity/Codex/OpenCode/Cursor-CLI) are **never** affected. Full catalog of the 7 gated templated files + 1 first-seed `marimo.toml`: [docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md](docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md).
114	
115	**Hard rules**:
116	
117	- Do **not** gate anything under `dot_config/nvim/` — Neovim is inherently vim by design.
118	- Do **not** gate editor configs (`.chezmoitemplates/editor/`, `dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl`, `dot_config/opencode/modify_*.json.tmpl`, `dot_cursor/modify_cli-config.json`) — the flag's semantic is shells + tmux only. Editors want vim → install the editor's vim extension.
119	- Do **not** broaden the gate to `bindkey -M viins`/`vicmd` calls inside `dot_config/zsh/tools/*.zsh` — harmless no-ops without zsh-vi-mode loaded.
120	- The `minimal` bundle in `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py` forces `enableVimMode = False` (CI/Docker). Don't change without explicit user request.
121	- New vim-touched file → follow the "Yes, gate it" / "No, leave it alone" flow in `docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md` → "For maintainers", and add it to the catalog table in that same page.
122	
123	### Install vs upgrade is split on purpose
124	
125	`chezmoi apply` + ansible is **install-only** (`state: present`, `creates:`). Explicit upgrade path: [`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh`](scripts/upgrade_tools.sh) via `just upgrade-*`. `scripts/**` is in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`, so the upgrade script runs from the repo, never deployed.
126	
127	**Hard rules**:
128	
129	- Do **not** rewrite ansible roles to `state: latest`.
130	- Do **not** add `apt upgrade` / system package bumps to default scope.
131	- **Minimum-version exception**: a role MAY auto-upgrade a single tool inside `chezmoi apply` when it legitimately needs a newer version (e.g. `python_uv_tools` needs `uv >= 0.8.5` for `--with-executables-from`). MUST detect install style (brew vs curl/standalone) and dispatch — never blindly `uv self update` (no-op on brew uv) or `brew upgrade uv` (errors if not a brew formula). Dispatch helper is mirrored in `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh::cat_uv()` and `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/tasks/main.yml`. See [docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md](docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md), [pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md](pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md), [pitfalls/ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip.md](pitfalls/ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip.md).
132	- **`with_executables_from:` entries MUST also declare `extra_binaries:`** in `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml`. Without it the install guard short-circuits on hosts where the primary binary already exists, and entry-point shims are never written (silent missing `jupyter` / `jupyter-notebook` despite `jupyter-lab` present). Audit: `yq '.python_uv_tools[] | select(.with_executables_from) | select(.extra_binaries == null) | .name' …` MUST print nothing. See [pitfalls/uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md](pitfalls/uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md).
133	- New upgrade category: [docs/this_repo/upgrades.md → Adding a new category](docs/this_repo/upgrades.md). For a tool already managed by brew/uv/npm/cargo/dotnet/gem/mise: do nothing — generic `upgrade` picks it up.
134	
135	### Sudo session is shared across all run-scripts
136	
137	All three `run_*` scripts share one sudo session via `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` — user prompted once at `chezmoi apply` start, reused silently downstream.
138	
139	**Hard rules**:
140	
141	- Do **not** re-implement `sudo -k` / `sudo -v` / TTY-read logic. Call the shared helper.
142	- Do **not** run `sudo -k` (invalidates the cache for the whole flow).
143	- Do **not** register a `trap … EXIT` that removes state (next run-script needs it).
144	- Do **not** read the password into a shell variable. Always `sudo -S <file`.
145	- Do **not** replace `_sudo_spawn_watchdog`'s `setsid`/`nohup` fallback with bare `setsid` — macOS lacks `setsid(1)` in base, the backgrounded failure is silent (redirected to `/dev/null`), and every run-script then re-prompts because `_sudo_state_valid`'s `kill -0` probe finds a dead PID. See [`pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md`](pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md).
146	
147	**Adding a new sudo surface in a run-script**:
148	
149	1. `{{ include "scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh" }}` near the top of the template.
150	2. Set the `NEED_SUDO` template flag.
151	3. Call `sudo_session_init "yourlabel"`; branch on return code + `sudo_session_skip_reason`.
152	4. Privileged commands via `sudo_run …` or `-e @$CHEZMOI_ANSIBLE_BECOME_FILE` for ansible.
153	
154	**Non-interactive password injection** (used by `scripts/fleet/apply.py` over SSH): `sudo_session_init` adopts `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` (a 0600 file) instead of prompting on `/dev/tty`. **Never** read `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` directly — always go through `sudo_session_init`. Full API + state + cleanup model: [docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md](docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md).
155	
156	### fleet-apply counter-intuitive defaults
157	
158	Full docs: [`docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md). Load-bearing invariants:
159	
160	- **`drift` ≠ `failed`**. When chezmoi can't prompt to overwrite a hand-edited file (no PTY over SSH), the host shows yellow ⚠ `drift` with paths listed — but it does **not** count toward exit code. Don't auto-"fix" drift unless asked. Resolution: hand-fix the remote, or `--force` to let template win.
161	- **`fleet-apply-file PATH` skips `run_*` scripts** (uses `chezmoi apply --exclude=scripts`). Ansible / Brewfile changes will NOT execute — use full `fleet-apply` for ansible iterations.
162	- **`--branch BRANCH` is no-op on local hosts** (the local source dir IS the user's editor working tree). Local hosts log warn and run against working tree as-is. The flag also forces mode to `apply`.
163	- **Install-only by design** (inherits the previous invariant). `just upgrade-*` must run on each host; fleet-apply does NOT broadcast upgrades.
164	- **Process substitution + sentinel are load-bearing**: `> >(tee -a $log) 2>&1 & _cz_pid=$!; wait $_cz_pid; _rc=$?; echo $_rc > $sentinel`. `--status` / `--tail` / `--watch` + SIGHUP trap depend on `$_cz_pid` pointing to chezmoi, not tee. Don't change to a pipeline.
165	- **Conservative drift classifier**: `_classify_drift()` only downgrades stderr lines matching the exact `chezmoi: <path>: could not open a new TTY: open /dev/tty:` fingerprint. Anything unrecognised stays `failed`. Don't broaden without explicit user request — silent downgrades hide real errors.
166	- **`fleet-status` ≠ `fleet-apply-status`** — easy to confuse:
167	  - `just fleet-status` → **pre-flight readiness probe** (states: `up-to-date`, `behind`, `ahead`, `dirty`, `drift`, `ready-to-update`, `busy`, `init-in-progress`, `toml-mismatch`, `not-init`, `no-source`, `no-chezmoi`, `unreachable`). Run **before** `fleet-apply`. Always exits 0; use `--readiness-json | jq` for scripted gates. `fleet-status-quick` skips remote `git fetch`.
168	  - `just fleet-apply-status` → **process-liveness probe** of `~/.cache/fleet-apply/<host>.{pid,sentinel,log}`. Run **during/after**. Pairs with `fleet-apply-tail` / `fleet-apply-watch` / `fleet-apply-kill`.
169	  - `toml-mismatch` catches a remote's `chezmoi.toml` missing prompt keys that current `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` requires, via static `_PROMPT_KEY_RE` comparison — `chezmoi dump-config` cannot be used (would re-evaluate the very template we're inspecting).
170	  - `fleet-edit` + `fleet-status` are forgiving (auto-seed / exit 0 with hint); `fleet-apply` keeps strict exit-2 on missing inventory. Don't unify.
171	
172	### `modify_` and `create_` prefix semantics
173	
174	- **`modify_`** files are executable scripts: chezmoi pipes current target contents to stdin, expects new contents on stdout. Used for `~/.claude/settings.json` (jq overlay), editor `settings.json` (VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity), agent CLI configs (`~/.cursor/cli-config.json`, `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`, `~/.codex/config.toml`), and `~/.gitconfig` (preserves `[credential "<URL>"]` blocks injected by `gh auth setup-git` so the gh-managed absolute path to the local `gh` binary — different on Intel mac / Apple Silicon / Linuxbrew — survives `chezmoi apply`). **Never** `chezmoi add` a `modify_` target — it would overwrite the script with the live file.
175	- **`create_`** files seed once; chezmoi never touches contents after. Used for `~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json` and editor `keybindings.json`. Refresh baseline by copying directly: `cp <target> "$(chezmoi source-path <target>)"`. `chezmoi add` strips the prefix; `chezmoi re-add` silently skips.
176	
177	Case studies + presence-gating in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`: [docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md). Three agent CLI overlays (incl. the Claude hook-aware merger that coexists with [CodeIsland](https://github.com/wxtsky/CodeIsland)'s auto-installed hook entries without ping-ponging): [docs/tools/agent-overlays.md](docs/tools/agent-overlays.md).
178	
179	### Tmux popup menu: ≥ 3.3 required + must fit terminal height
180	
181	The popup menu (bound to `prefix + Space` and `prefix + e`) is **generated** by `~/.config/tmux/menu.sh`, not inline in `keybindings.conf`. Two unrelated tmux quirks force this:
182	
183	1. **Position clamping (tmux ≥ 3.3)**: `display-menu -x R -y P` is silently suppressed on tmux 3.2a (Ubuntu 22.04 apt) when it would place the menu past the terminal edge. tmux 3.3+ clamps. `devtools` role auto-upgrades on Debian/Ubuntu (Linuxbrew first, else [`nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage`](https://github.com/nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage) extracted to `~/.local/share/tmux-appimage/` with a `~/.local/bin/tmux` shim). Run `tmux kill-server` once after — running servers keep the old binary in memory.
184	2. **Menu-too-tall silent failure (all versions)**: `display-menu` does **not** paginate. Taller than terminal → entire popup suppressed, no error, nothing in `tmux show-messages`. `man tmux`: _"If the menu is too large to fit on the terminal, it is not displayed."_ Misdiagnosed for hours as a CSI-u keysym bug after a 50-row flat menu started failing on smaller heights.
185	
186	**Hard rules**:
187	
188	- **Top menu cap ≈ 14 rows**. Generator reads `#{client_height}` and tier-trims; retest at heights 14 / 22 / 60 when changing tiers. Push lower-frequency items into category submenus.
189	- **Submenus = separate scripts**, each `exec tmux display-menu …`. Quoting context resets per script.
190	- **Complex commands** (anything with `{`, `}`, `;`, backticks, nested fzf binds) MUST live in their own script. tmux's parser treats `{}` / `;` as command-block delimiters even inside `'…'` inside `"…"`, silently aborting parse.
191	- **Test by shrinking the terminal vertically**. Full-height verification does not catch the height-fit failure.
192	
193	See `pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md` (red herrings included) and `pitfalls/yazi-tmux-popup-crash.md`.
194	
195	### Key tmux settings for coding agents
196	
197	Non-obvious settings other tools depend on; do not remove without checking:
198	
199	- `extended-keys on` + `terminal-features 'xterm*:extkeys'` — forwards Shift+Enter, Ctrl+Enter, Ctrl+/, Ctrl+digit to inner apps (Claude Code, Neovim, …). **Never use `always`** — re-encodes EVERY `Ctrl+letter` as CSI-u including the LF (Ctrl+J) embedded in pasted multi-line text → ble.sh inserts `^[[106;5u` literally instead of newline. See `pitfalls/tmux-extended-keys-always-paste.md`.
200	- `escape-time 0` — eliminates ESC delay for Neovim.
201	- `set-clipboard on` + `terminal-features …:clipboard` (for `xterm*`, `ghostty*`, `alacritty*`) — OSC 52 over SSH without terminfo `Ms`. Paired with SSH-conditional `vim.g.clipboard = vim.ui.clipboard.osc52` in `dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`. See [docs/tools/tmux/README.md → OSC 52 Clipboard](docs/tools/tmux/README.md).
202	- `allow-passthrough on` — OSC passthrough for terminal images.
203	- macOS terminals must send Option as Meta/Esc+ for `M-` keybindings (theme switching, layouts, fine resize). Ghostty/cmux: `macos-option-as-alt = left` in `dot_config/ghostty/config`. See [docs/tools/ghostty.md](docs/tools/ghostty.md).
204	
205	Full tmux config breakdown / theme switching / keybindings / troubleshooting: [docs/tools/tmux/](docs/tools/tmux/).
206	
207	### Zellij `default_mode "locked"`
208	
209	`dot_config/zellij/config.kdl` uses `default_mode "locked"` so all keys pass through to inner apps by default. `Ctrl+G` to unlock Zellij commands. First Zellij launch (no existing config): select the "Unlock-First (non-colliding)" keybinding preset.
210

## TMUX KEYBOARD-SHORTCUT NAMESPACE SURVEY

### 1. Prefix vs Root-Table Policy

**Policy statement**: CLAUDE.md line 24 establishes the convention:
> "Keybinding (`Ctrl+`/`Alt+`) in any tool config — Cross-check namespace before claiming — **tmux root-table `bind -n C-*` shadows inner apps; prefer `Alt+` for new actions**"

**Established convention** (from `common.conf.tmpl` and `keybindings.conf.tmpl`):
- **Prefix + letter bindings** are the primary namespace for interactive menu actions and session management
- **Root-table `C-<key>` bindings** are reserved for window switching (`C-1..9`, `C-0`) and vim-pane navigation (`C-h/j/k/l`). These **shadow inner apps intentionally** because they cross into Neovim/vim splits.
- **Root-table `M-<key>` (Alt) bindings** are preferred for menu-like actions that need to be accessible without prefix. Currently used for: layouts (`M-1..5`), resize (`M-h/j/k/l`), theme switching (`M-c`, `M-t`), copy operations (`M-y`, `M-i`), and help (`M-/`).

**Example existing bindings**:
- Prefix table: `prefix + g` (sesh picker), `prefix + G` (lazygit), `prefix + Space` (menu), `prefix + 0` (sesh-root), `prefix + 9` (scode)
- Root table: `C-1..9` (window switch), `C-0` (sesh-root), `C-h/j/k/l` (vim-tmux-navigator), `M-1..5` (layouts)

### 2. **SESSION/WINDOW/PANE KILL PATHS**

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Detach all clients of the current tmux session, then destroy the session.
session=$(tmux display-message -p '#S')
tmux detach-client -s "$session"
tmux kill-session -t "$session"
```

<tool-use data-tool-type="generic" data-tool-name="AskUserQuestion"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **AskUserQuestion**</summary>
**「Clean-quit 不要 restore」這個行為要套到哪些 kill 路徑?(目前的 kill 路徑包含:`prefix+x` 殺 pane、`prefix+W` 殺 window、`prefix+X` 殺 session、`prefix+M-x` 殺 session & exit、滑鼠右鍵選單裡的「Kill all sessions (server)」,還有 menu-session.sh 裡的全部 5 個變體)**

Options:
- **只在「Kill all sessions (server)」+「Kill session & exit 時是最後一個 session」(Recommended)** - 保守。Kill pane/window 不影響。一般 Kill session(其他 session 還在)也不清,因為 server 還活著 restore 不會觸發。只有真的要讓 server 死掉才清 `last`。一致符合『我故意關掉的 = 不要 restore』的直覺。
- **也包含一般的「Kill session」/「Kill session & exit」(無論是否最後一個)** - 更積極。任何 session 被殺都會清 `last` symlink。下次 server 重啟就完全不 restore(即使是 crash 也不會 restore)。
- **另外給一個新的 explicit「Quit tmux cleanly」入口,其餘維持不動** - 完全不動現有 kill 路徑,新增一個顯眼的「Clean quit」動作。需要『真的退出』時用這個。學習曲線高一點但隔離乾淨。

**三個右鍵選單(pane / window-tab / status-left session)的鍵盤捷徑要用哪一組?**

Options:
- **`Alt+p` / `Alt+w` / `Alt+s`(無 prefix,mnemonic)(Recommended)** - 符合 CLAUDE.md「prefer Alt+ for new actions」規則,零步驟 = 跟右鍵一樣零摩擦。風險:Alt+w 在 readline 是 copy-region-as-kill、Alt+p 是 history search,在 shell 中會被 tmux 攔下來。
- **`Alt+P` / `Alt+W` / `Alt+S`(大寫,需 Shift+Alt)** - 更少跟 readline / vim 的 Alt+小寫衝突,但 Shift+Alt+letter 在某些終端機(尤其 macOS)Option-as-Alt 設定下可能不通。
- **`prefix + Alt+p/w/s` (避開 root-table 命名空間)** - 需要按 prefix(`Ctrl+B`/你的自訂 prefix)再 Alt+letter。完全不會跟 inner apps 衝突,但少一個按鍵的右鍵替代品的快感。
- **繼承右鍵選單原始的 emoji 邏輯,只增加 prefix 入口** - 只在 prefix table 加 `prefix + ,` / `prefix + .` / `prefix + ;` 之類的標點(但 `,` 跟 tmux 內建 rename-window 衝突,`.` 跟 move-window 衝突,`;` 跟 last-pane 衝突)。基本上沒好位子,不建議。


**Answer:** 只在「Kill all sessions (server)」+「Kill session & exit 時是最後一個 session」(Recommended), `prefix + Alt+p/w/s` (避開 root-table 命名空間)

# tmux: 解決「主動關掉 session 也會 auto-restore」+ 三個右鍵選單上鍵盤

## Context

`dot_config/tmux/common.conf.tmpl:16` 設 `@continuum-restore 'on'`,tmux-continuum 每 15 分鐘存一次快照到 `~/.local/share/tmux/resurrect/last`(symlink),並在**每次 tmux server 啟動且無 session 時無條件 auto-restore**。它無法分辨「使用者主動 `kill-server` / 殺掉最後一個 session」vs「crash / reboot」。使用者選擇方案 B:**保留 auto-restore 當作 crash 保險絲,但給「真的要退出」的路徑一個明確的清理出口**。

同時,目前三組右鍵選單(pane / window-tab / status-left session)的 menu body 是 inline 在 `keybindings.conf.tmpl` 的 `MouseDown3*` 綁定裡,沒有鍵盤對應,使用者想加上 `prefix + Alt+p/w/s` 觸發。

## Decisions (使用者已確認)

- **Clean scope**: 只在「Kill all sessions (server)」+「Kill session & exit 時是最後一個 session」這兩條路徑清理 `last` symlink。`kill-pane` / `kill-window` / 一般 `kill-session`(其他 session 還在 → server 不會死 → 不會觸發 restore)維持不動。
- **鍵盤對應**: `prefix + Alt+p` (pane) / `prefix + Alt+w` (window) / `prefix + Alt+s` (status-left session menu),避開 root-table 命名空間。

## Approach

### Part A — Clean-quit 出口

**新增** 共用 helper `dot_config/tmux/executable_resurrect-forget.sh`:
\```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Remove tmux-resurrect's "last" symlink so the next tmux server start does
# NOT auto-restore via tmux-continuum. Periodic save will re-create it later.
# Used by "Kill server" and "Kill session & exit (last session)" paths only.
set -euo pipefail
rm -f "${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/tmux/resurrect/last"
\```

**修改** `dot_config/tmux/executable_kill-session-exit.sh` — 在 kill 之前數 session 數,如果這是最後一個就先呼叫 `resurrect-forget.sh`:
\```bash
session=$(tmux display-message -p '#S')
session_count=$(tmux list-sessions -F '#S' 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
if [ "$session_count" -le 1 ]; then
  "$HOME/.config/tmux/resurrect-forget.sh"
fi
tmux detach-client -s "$session"
tmux kill-session -t "$session"
\```

**新增** `dot_config/tmux/executable_kill-server-clean.sh`:
\```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Clean tmux quit: clear resurrect/last so next start has nothing to auto-restore.
set -euo pipefail
"$HOME/.config/tmux/resurrect-forget.sh"
tmux kill-server
\```

**修改入口點** — 把目前直接呼叫 `kill-server` 的兩個地方換成新 wrapper:
- `dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl:~109` 的 `MouseDown3StatusLeft` 選單裡 `"Kill all sessions" Q { confirm-before -p "..." kill-server }` → 改呼叫 `run-shell "$HOME/.config/tmux/kill-server-clean.sh"`
- `dot_config/tmux/executable_menu-session.sh:23` 的 `"Kill all sessions" Q "confirm-before -p '...' kill-server"` → 同上

`kill-session-exit.sh` 的修改自動覆蓋下列三個入口(都已經呼叫該 script,不必改):
- `keybindings.conf.tmpl` 的 `prefix + M-x` 綁定
- `MouseDown3StatusLeft` 的 "Kill session & exit" 條目
- `menu-session.sh:22` 的 "Kill session & exit" 條目

### Part B — 三個右鍵選單的鍵盤觸發

**萃取** 三個 menu body 出來成獨立 script,沿用倉庫現有的 `executable_menu-*.sh` 模式。每個 script 接受第一個參數 `mouse` / `key` 決定 `-x` / `-y` 定位(mouse 用 `M`,key 用 `P` = current pane):

- 新增 `dot_config/tmux/executable_menu-pane.sh` — 內容來自 `keybindings.conf.tmpl:23-46` 的 pane menu(13 列,Split/swap/resize/zoom/Kill pane 等)
- 新增 `dot_config/tmux/executable_menu-window.sh` — 內容來自 `keybindings.conf.tmpl:50-92` 的 window-tab menu(23 列,layout/rename/bookmark/Kill window 等;注意這個已經接近 tmux ≥ 3.3 popup 高度上限,Part B 不增加列數)
- 新增 `dot_config/tmux/executable_menu-status-left.sh` — 內容來自 `keybindings.conf.tmpl:94-110` 的 session menu(11 列,next/prev/rename/move/Kill session & exit/Kill all sessions(改用 kill-server-clean))

**改寫** `MouseDown3Pane` / `MouseDown3Status` / `MouseDown3StatusLeft` 三個綁定,讓它們 `run-shell "$HOME/.config/tmux/menu-<X>.sh mouse"`(`MouseDown3Pane` 保留外層的 `if-shell` copy-mode 偵測,只把 menu body 那一段換掉)。

**新增** 三個 prefix keybinding 在 `keybindings.conf.tmpl`(放在現有 menu 區塊附近):
\```tmux
bind -T prefix M-p run-shell "$HOME/.config/tmux/menu-pane.sh key"
bind -T prefix M-w run-shell "$HOME/.config/tmux/menu-window.sh key"
bind -T prefix M-s run-shell "$HOME/.config/tmux/menu-status-left.sh key"
\```

**Pitfall 風險**: tmux popup 在內容超過終端高度時會「整個靜默不顯示」(已記錄在 CLAUDE.md "Tmux popup menu" 規則 + `pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md`)。window-tab menu 已經 23 列,鍵盤觸發在小終端機上會看不到。可接受:這個 plan 不擴增任何列數,只是改變觸發方式;mouse 觸發本來在小終端也會 silent fail,並無 regression。文件提醒在 cheatsheet 加註。

## Files to modify / create

**新增** (4 個 helper script + 3 個 menu script,共 7 個):
- `dot_config/tmux/executable_resurrect-forget.sh`
- `dot_config/tmux/executable_kill-server-clean.sh`
- `dot_config/tmux/executable_menu-pane.sh`
- `dot_config/tmux/executable_menu-window.sh`
- `dot_config/tmux/executable_menu-status-left.sh`

**修改**:
- `dot_config/tmux/executable_kill-session-exit.sh` — last-session 偵測 + 呼叫 resurrect-forget
- `dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl` — 三個 MouseDown3* 改用 run-shell 委派;新增 prefix M-p/w/s 三個綁定;MouseDown3StatusLeft 的 "Kill all sessions" 改用 kill-server-clean
- `dot_config/tmux/executable_menu-session.sh` — "Kill all sessions" entry 改用 kill-server-clean

## Cross-file maintenance (per CLAUDE.md)

- `docs/shells/keybindings.md` — 加 `prefix + M-p` / `prefix + M-w` / `prefix + M-s` 三列(每列含 trigger / scope / 對應 mouse event / 一行描述)。同時補上 `kill-server-clean.sh` / `resurrect-forget.sh` 的行為說明。
- `dot_config/tmux/cheatsheet.md` — 在 menu / kill 區塊加上新的鍵與行為註記(含 popup-too-tall 提醒)。
- `docs/tools/tmux/` (`README.md` 或對應頁)— 加一段「Continuum auto-restore 與 clean quit」說明,點出 `last` symlink 機制、哪兩個入口會清掉、何時不會(crash / reboot / 一般 kill-session 仍會 restore)。
- `pitfalls/tmux-continuum-restores-on-intentional-quit.md`(新增)— 紀錄這個 trap 的症狀(主動關掉也會 restore)+ 根因(continuum 無法分辨意圖)+ 解法(雙路徑清理 `last` symlink)+ 為什麼不全面關掉 auto-restore(crash 救援)。
- 不需要動 `CLAUDE.md` 的 Hard rules — 沒有新的跨檔不變式;沒有觸碰 workmux 6 檔。

## Verification

1. `chezmoi apply --dry-run` — 確認新 script 的 executable_ 前綴生效,沒有 template 錯誤。
2. `chezmoi apply` 後 `tmux source-file ~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf` — syntax check(per CLAUDE.md「validate app configs with the app」hard rule)。
3. **滑鼠右鍵 regression test**: 對 pane / window-tab / status-left session 各右鍵一次,確認選單還是出來且內容跟改動前一致。
4. **鍵盤觸發**: `prefix + M-p` / `M-w` / `M-s` 各按一次,確認三個選單出現在 pane 中央。
5. **Clean-quit 行為驗證** (在乾淨環境):
   - 建立兩個 session(`tmux new -s a`, `tmux new -s b`),在 `a` 跑 `prefix + M-x` confirm Y;檢查 `ls -la ~/.local/share/tmux/resurrect/last` — **應該還在**(因為 `b` 還活著)。
   - 然後在 `b` 跑 `prefix + M-x` confirm Y;檢查 `last` — **應該被刪除**(最後一個 session)。
   - `tmux new -s c`, 從 status-left menu 選 "Kill all sessions" confirm Y;檢查 `last` — **應該被刪除**。
   - 上述每次清理後 `tmux` 重新進入,確認**沒有 auto-restore**(該是空的)。
6. **Crash 救援仍存在**: 跑一陣子讓 continuum 至少存一次(15min,或手動 `prefix + Ctrl-s`),`pkill -9 tmux: server` 模擬 crash,重新 `tmux` — 應該照舊 auto-restore。
7. **小終端 popup-fit**: 把終端機高度縮到 ~15 列,試 `prefix + M-w`(window menu 23 列),確認知道會看不到(預期 silent fail,在 cheatsheet / pitfall 有紀錄)。

## Out of scope

- 不關掉 `@continuum-restore 'on'`(這是方案 A,使用者沒選)。
- 不修改 `kill-pane` / `kill-window` / 一般 `kill-session`(維持「只有真的退出才清」的最小擾動)。
- 不刪除 `~/.local/share/tmux/resurrect/` 底下歷史檔案(只動 `last` symlink,讓 crash recovery 還能用 manual restore `prefix + Ctrl-r` 撈回)。
- 不改 `@continuum-save-interval`。

bind -T prefix M-s run-shell "$HOME/.config/tmux/menu-status-left.sh key"
```

**Pitfall 風險**: tmux popup 在內容超過終端高度時會「整個靜默不顯示」(已記錄在 CLAUDE.md "Tmux popup menu" 規則 + `pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md`)。window-tab menu 已經 23 列,鍵盤觸發在小終端機上會看不到。可接受:這個 plan 不擴增任何列數,只是改變觸發方式;mouse 觸發本來在小終端也會 silent fail,並無 regression。文件提醒在 cheatsheet 加註。

- `docs/shells/keybindings.md` — 加 `prefix + M-p` / `prefix + M-w` / `prefix + M-s` 三列(每列含 trigger / scope / 對應 mouse event / 一行描述)。同時補上 `kill-server-clean.sh` / `resurrect-forget.sh` 的行為說明。
- `dot_config/tmux/cheatsheet.md` — 在 menu / kill 區塊加上新的鍵與行為註記(含 popup-too-tall 提醒)。
- `docs/tools/tmux/` (`README.md` 或對應頁)— 加一段「Continuum auto-restore 與 clean quit」說明,點出 `last` symlink 機制、哪兩個入口會清掉、何時不會(crash / reboot / 一般 kill-session 仍會 restore)。
- `pitfalls/tmux-continuum-restores-on-intentional-quit.md`(新增)— 紀錄這個 trap 的症狀(主動關掉也會 restore)+ 根因(continuum 無法分辨意圖)+ 解法(雙路徑清理 `last` symlink)+ 為什麼不全面關掉 auto-restore(crash 救援)。
- 不需要動 `CLAUDE.md` 的 Hard rules — 沒有新的跨檔不變式;沒有觸碰 workmux 6 檔。

## Verification

1. `chezmoi apply --dry-run` — 確認新 script 的 executable_ 前綴生效,沒有 template 錯誤。
2. `chezmoi apply` 後 `tmux source-file ~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf` — syntax check(per CLAUDE.md「validate app configs with the app」hard rule)。
3. **滑鼠右鍵 regression test**: 對 pane / window-tab / status-left session 各右鍵一次,確認選單還是出來且內容跟改動前一致。
4. **鍵盤觸發**: `prefix + M-p` / `M-w` / `M-s` 各按一次,確認三個選單出現在 pane 中央。
5. **Clean-quit 行為驗證** (在乾淨環境):
   - 建立兩個 session(`tmux new -s a`, `tmux new -s b`),在 `a` 跑 `prefix + M-x` confirm Y;檢查 `ls -la ~/.local/share/tmux/resurrect/last` — **應該還在**(因為 `b` 還活著)。
   - 然後在 `b` 跑 `prefix + M-x` confirm Y;檢查 `last` — **應該被刪除**(最後一個 session)。
   - `tmux new -s c`, 從 status-left menu 選 "Kill all sessions" confirm Y;檢查 `last` — **應該被刪除**。
   - 上述每次清理後 `tmux` 重新進入,確認**沒有 auto-restore**(該是空的)。
6. **Crash 救援仍存在**: 跑一陣子讓 continuum 至少存一次(15min,或手動 `prefix + Ctrl-s`),`pkill -9 tmux: server` 模擬 crash,重新 `tmux` — 應該照舊 auto-restore。
7. **小終端 popup-fit**: 把終端機高度縮到 ~15 列,試 `prefix + M-w`(window menu 23 列),確認知道會看不到(預期 silent fail,在 cheatsheet / pitfall 有紀錄)。

## Out of scope

- 不關掉 `@continuum-restore 'on'`(這是方案 A,使用者沒選)。
- 不修改 `kill-pane` / `kill-window` / 一般 `kill-session`(維持「只有真的退出才清」的最小擾動)。
- 不刪除 `~/.local/share/tmux/resurrect/` 底下歷史檔案(只動 `last` symlink,讓 crash recovery 還能用 manual restore `prefix + Ctrl-r` 撈回)。
- 不改 `@continuum-save-interval`。

131	# Requires OSC 133 markers from the shell — emitted by

133	# e.g. `sh`, `bash` without our hook, or `DISABLE_OSC133=1`), these keys are
134	# no-ops. tmux 3.4+ required for next-prompt/previous-prompt; the `-o` variant
135	# (jump to output start, not prompt start) is tmux 3.5+.
136	#
137	#   {  / }    previous/next prompt (the prompt line itself)
138	#   M-[ / M-] previous/next command output (line AFTER the prompt — usually
139	#             what you want for "skip to the output of the previous command")
140	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
141	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} '{' send-keys -X previous-prompt
142	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} '}' send-keys -X next-prompt
143	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} M-[ send-keys -X previous-prompt -o
144	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} M-] send-keys -X next-prompt -o

150	# prefix + y: copy visible pane content to system clipboard

152	# terminal via OSC 52 (requires `set-clipboard on` in common.conf). This works
153	# over SSH without shelling out to pbcopy/xclip on the remote host.
154	bind y run-shell "tmux capture-pane -p | tmux load-buffer -w - && tmux display-message 'Pane content copied to clipboard'"
155	
156	# prefix + Y: copy full scrollback to system clipboard
157	bind Y run-shell "tmux capture-pane -pS - | tmux load-buffer -w - && tmux display-message 'Full scrollback copied to clipboard'"

163	    | tmux load-buffer -w - && tmux display-message 'Selected lines copied'"
164

166	# Requires OSC 133 markers — if the shell doesn't emit them (non-zsh shell,

168	# empty. Chain: enter copy-mode, jump to start of previous command's output,
169	# begin selection, jump forward to the next prompt (end of output), copy,
170	# flash confirmation.
171	bind M-y copy-mode \; \
172	  send-keys -X previous-prompt -o \; \
173	  send-keys -X begin-selection \; \
174	  send-keys -X next-prompt \; \
175	  send-keys -X copy-pipe-and-cancel "tmux load-buffer -w -" \; \

```text
1	# tmux: nested display-menu via `run-shell` from a right-click parent menu is unreliable
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section): submenu flashes and disappears, popup in bottom-right corner, `display-menu` flickers, right-click submenu won't stay open, tmux menu position wrong from status bar, submenu opens but selecting an item does nothing on second invocation
4	**First seen**: 2026-04
5	**Affects**: tmux 3.3+ (likely older too); any `display-menu` invoked indirectly via `run-shell "$HOME/.config/tmux/menu-foo.sh"` from a `MouseDown3*` parent
6	**Status**: workaround — inline the submenu items into the parent instead of nesting via shell script
7	
8	## Symptom
9	
10	A `tmux display-menu` submenu (e.g. `~/.config/tmux/menu-layouts.sh`) behaves
11	two different ways depending on how it's invoked:
12	
13	- From a keyboard popup menu (e.g. `prefix + Enter` → "Layouts..."): opens
14	  near the cursor / pane center, stays open until an item is chosen. **Works.**
15	- From a **right-click status-bar** menu (e.g. right-click window tab →
16	  "Layouts..."): pops up in the **bottom-right corner of the terminal** and
17	  often **flashes away after a fraction of a second** before any item can be
18	  picked. Sometimes (if you happen to mouse over a row immediately) it stays.
19	
20	No error in `tmux show-messages`. The bind is correctly wired — `prefix +
21	Enter` path proves the script runs.
22	
23	## Root cause
24	
25	Two unrelated `display-menu` quirks stacked on top of each other:
26	
27	### 1. Mouse-release dismiss (the "flash and gone")
28	
29	A submenu without `-O` closes on the **next mouse event** that isn't a hover.
30	The right-click on the parent window-tab generated a pending mouse-release /
31	mouse-move event in tmux's event queue. The parent menu used `-O` (Open)
32	so it survived; the submenu didn't, so the queued release event hit it
33	immediately and dismissed it. With keyboard invocation there is no pending
34	mouse event, so the same submenu stayed open.
35	
36	### 2. `-x R -y P` from a status-bar event lands at bottom-right
37	
38	`-x R` = right edge of the pane. `-y P` = the line of the cursor's pane.
39	When `display-menu` is launched from a `MouseDown3Status` binding, "the
40	cursor's pane line" resolves to the **status bar row** (very bottom of the
41	terminal). Combined with `-x R` you get a popup glued to the bottom-right
42	corner. tmux 3.3+ then clamps it to fit on screen, which makes it look
43	"stuck" there. From a keyboard popup the cursor is in a normal pane, so the
44	same `-x R -y P` puts the menu in a sensible place near the parent.
45	
46	`man tmux` on `display-menu`:
47	> `M` for the mouse position, `W` for the window position on the status line,
48	> `S` for the line above or below the status line, `C` for the centre of the
49	> client.
50	
51	## Fix
52	
53	**Don't nest.** Inline the submenu items directly into the parent menu, even
54	if it pushes the parent above the ~14-row soft cap (see
55	`AGENTS.md` → "tmux ≥ 3.3 required for popup menu"). The cap exists for a
56	real reason (small terminals silently suppress oversized menus), so when
57	inlining grows the parent past 14 rows, drop the lowest-frequency rows and
58	move them to the keyboard popup (`prefix + Enter` → submenu) where the
59	nesting works fine.
60	
61	```tmux
62	# Bad: nested via run-shell (selection silently no-ops on 2nd invocation)
63	bind-key -n MouseDown3Status display-menu -O ... \
64	  "Layouts..." L { run-shell "~/.config/tmux/menu-layouts.sh" } \
65	  ...
66	
67	# Good: inline the layout commands directly
68	bind-key -n MouseDown3Status display-menu -O ... \
69	  "Even horizontal" 1 { select-layout even-horizontal } \
70	  "Even vertical"   2 { select-layout even-vertical } \
71	  "Tiled (grid)"    5 { select-layout tiled } \
72	  ...
73	```
74	
75	The keyboard popup path (`prefix + Enter` → "Layouts..." → `run-shell
76	~/.config/tmux/menu-layouts.sh`) keeps working — the bug is specific to
77	mouse-driven parents whose mouse-event lifecycle interferes with the child
78	menu's input handling.
79	
80	## Things that look like fixes but aren't
81	
82	Spent time trying these — none worked reliably across "first invocation"
83	vs "after cancelling once":
84	
85	- `-O` on the submenu: stops the immediate flash-and-gone, but on second
86	  invocation after cancelling the parent, selecting an item silently
87	  no-ops.
88	- `-x M -y M` on the submenu: fixes the bottom-right placement, but mouse
89	  position state is stale after cancel-and-retry, so it pops up in
90	  unpredictable places.
91	- `run-shell -d 0.1 "~/.config/tmux/menu-foo.sh"`: deferring the shell
92	  exec lets the parent's mouse-release drain, fixes the flash, but the
93	  selection-no-ops bug remains.
94	- `display-popup` wrapping the submenu: changes mouse semantics entirely
95	  but you lose `display-menu`'s key shortcuts.
96	
97	The man page (tmux 3.3+) explains why `-O` alone isn't enough:
98	
99	> If the mouse is enabled and the menu is opened from a mouse key binding,
100	> releasing the mouse button … closes the menu. `-M` tells tmux the menu
101	> should handle mouse events; by default only menus opened from mouse key
102	> bindings do so.
103	
104	A submenu launched via `run-shell` is NOT considered "opened from a mouse
105	key binding" — so `-M` doesn't help either, and the trailing mouse events
106	from the now-defunct parent leak into an undefined input state for the
107	child.
108	
109	## Related
110	
111	- `pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md` — different silent failure mode
112	  for the same `display-menu` command (height clamping / menu-too-tall).
113
```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Remove tmux-resurrect's "last" symlink so the next tmux server start does NOT
# auto-restore via tmux-continuum (@continuum-restore 'on' in common.conf).
# Periodic save (every 15 min by default) will re-create it after restore.
# Only the symlink is removed — historical snapshots stay, so `prefix + Ctrl-r`
# manual restore still works if you change your mind.
#
# Wired into:
#   - executable_kill-server-clean.sh   (always clears)
#   - executable_kill-session-exit.sh   (clears only when this is the last
#                                        surviving session, i.e. the server
#                                        is about to die)
set -euo pipefail
target="${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/tmux/resurrect/last"
rm -f -- "$target"

```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Clean tmux quit: forget tmux-resurrect's "last" symlink, then kill the server.
# Goal: stop tmux-continuum's @continuum-restore from re-attaching the just-
# closed sessions on the next tmux start. Used by the "Kill all sessions"
# entries in:
#   - keybindings.conf.tmpl::MouseDown3StatusLeft (status-left right-click menu)
#   - executable_menu-session.sh                  (prefix+Space → Session mgmt)
# Crash recovery is unaffected — historical resurrect snapshots stay on disk
# and `prefix + Ctrl-r` can still restore them manually.
set -euo pipefail
"$HOME/.config/tmux/resurrect-forget.sh"
tmux kill-server

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Top-level tmux popup menu — invoked by `prefix + Space`.
3	#
4	# Why a script (not inline `display-menu` in keybindings.conf):
5	#   1. tmux's command parser stops at literal `;`, `{`, `}` even inside
6	#      nested quotes. With ~50 menu rows full of fzf binds and shell
7	#      one-liners, escaping became fragile and broke silently.
8	#   2. tmux `display-menu` does not paginate. If the menu is taller than
9	#      the terminal, the entire popup is suppressed with no error. By
10	#      generating the menu here we can read $TMUX client_height and
11	#      auto-trim low-frequency rows when small.
12	#   3. Submenus are normal `tmux display-menu` invocations from rows;
13	#      they don't share quoting context with the parent menu.
14	#
15	# Submenus live in sibling scripts:
16	#   menu-layouts.sh, menu-session.sh, menu-sesh.sh,
17	#   menu-popups.sh, menu-theme.sh, menu-system.sh, menu-agents.sh
18	#
19	# See: pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-parse-failure.md
20	
21	set -euo pipefail
22	
23	H=$(tmux display-message -p '#{client_height}')
24	DIR=~/.config/tmux
25	
26	# Tier 0: ALWAYS shown (highest frequency, ~7 rows + 2 separators)
27	declare -a tier0=(
28	  "Last window"  Tab "last-window"
29	  "Last pane"    P   "last-pane"
30	  ""             ""  ""
31	  "Choose win"   w   "choose-tree -Zw"
32	  "Choose sess"  s   "choose-tree -Zs"
33	  "Pane #s"      q   "display-panes -d 0"
34	  ""             ""  ""
35	  "Sesh picker"  g   "run-shell '$DIR/sesh-picker.sh'"
36	  "Lazygit"      G   "display-popup -E -w 90% -h 90% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' lazygit ' 'lazygit'"
37	)
38	
39	# Tier 1: shown when height >= 22 (adds new-window/split/zoom)
40	declare -a tier1=(
41	  ""             ""  ""
42	  "New window"   c   "new-window -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
43	  "Split |"      "|" "split-window -h -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
44	  "Split -"      "-" "split-window -v -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
45	  "Zoom"         z   "resize-pane -Z"
46	)
47	
48	# Tier 2: submenus + cheatsheet (always shown if Tier 1 is shown)
49	declare -a tier2=(
50	  ""             ""  ""
51	  "→ Layouts"    L   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-layouts.sh'"
52	  "→ Session"    S   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-session.sh'"
53	  "→ Sesh+"      E   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-sesh.sh'"
54	  "→ Agents"     A   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-agents.sh'"
55	  "→ Popups"     o   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-popups.sh'"
56	  "→ Theme"      T   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-theme.sh'"
57	  "→ System"     Y   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-system.sh'"
58	  ""             ""  ""
59	  "Cheatsheet"   "?" "display-popup -E -w 80% -h 80% -T ' tmux cheatsheet ' 'glow -p $DIR/cheatsheet.md 2>/dev/null || less $DIR/cheatsheet.md'"
60	  "Search keys"  "/" "run-shell -b ~/.tmux/plugins/tmux-fzf/scripts/keybinding.sh"
61	)
62	
63	rows=("${tier0[@]}")
64	if [ "$H" -ge 22 ]; then
65	  rows+=("${tier1[@]}" "${tier2[@]}")
66	elif [ "$H" -ge 14 ]; then
67	  rows+=("${tier2[@]}")
68	fi
69	
70	exec tmux display-menu -T "#[align=centre,bold]tmux (h=$H)" -x R -y P "${rows[@]}"
71

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Pane right-click menu, invocable from the keyboard via `prefix + M-p`.
# Mirrors the inline body of `MouseDown3Pane` in keybindings.conf.tmpl.
#
# WHY a separate copy (not extracted from the mouse binding):
#   pitfalls/tmux-submenu-flash-and-bottom-right.md — a `display-menu`
#   launched indirectly via `run-shell` from a `MouseDown3*` binding is
#   not treated as "opened from a mouse key binding" by tmux, so the
#   queued mouse-release event dismisses it (flash-and-gone). Therefore
#   the mouse path MUST stay inline. Keyboard activation has no such
#   queued event, so a script wrapper is safe here.
#
# *** IF YOU EDIT THE MENU ITEMS, ALSO UPDATE ***
#     dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl :: MouseDown3Pane
set -euo pipefail

declare -a rows=(
  "Horizontal Split" h "split-window -h -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
  "Vertical Split"   v "split-window -v -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
  "" "" ""
  "Swap Up"    u "swap-pane -U"
  "Swap Down"  d "swap-pane -D"
  "Swap Left"  l "swap-pane -t '{left-of}'"
  "Swap Right" r "swap-pane -t '{right-of}'"
  "" "" ""
  "#{?window_zoomed_flag,Unzoom,Zoom}" z "resize-pane -Z"
  "Resize 75%"  "+" "resize-pane -x 75%"
  "Resize even" "=" "select-layout even-horizontal"
  "Mark pane"   m "select-pane -m"
  "Swap marked" s "swap-pane"
  "Join marked pane here (h-split)" j "join-pane -h ; display-message 'Joined marked pane here'"
  "Join marked pane here (v-split)" J "join-pane -v ; display-message 'Joined marked pane here'"
  "Send pane to window... (h-split)" S "choose-tree -Zw -F '#{window_name}' \"join-pane -h -s '#{pane_id}' -t '%%' ; display-message 'Sent pane to target'\""
  "Break to new window" B "break-pane ; display-message 'Broke pane out to window #{window_index} (#{window_name})'"
  "" "" ""
  "Enter copy mode" "[" "copy-mode"
  "Respawn"     R "respawn-pane -k"
  "Kill pane"   X "confirm-before -p 'Kill pane? (y/n)' kill-pane"
)

exec tmux display-menu -T "#[align=centre]#{pane_current_command} (pane #{pane_index})" -x R -y P "${rows[@]}"

```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Window-tab right-click menu, invocable from the keyboard via `prefix + M-w`.
# Mirrors the inline body of `MouseDown3Status` in keybindings.conf.tmpl.
#
# WHY a separate copy: see header of executable_menu-pane.sh.
#
# *** IF YOU EDIT THE MENU ITEMS, ALSO UPDATE ***
#     dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl :: MouseDown3Status
#
# WARNING — height: this menu is 23 visible rows. `display-menu` silently
# suppresses itself if it can't fit on screen. On terminals ≲ 26 rows the
# menu will not appear. Mouse-right-click has the same limitation; this
# script just changes the trigger. See pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md
# for the height-clamping behavior.
set -euo pipefail

declare -a rows=(
  "Swap Left"  l "swap-window -t :-1"
  "Swap Right" r "swap-window -t :+1"
  "" "" ""
  "Even horizontal" 1 "select-layout even-horizontal"
  "Even vertical"   2 "select-layout even-vertical"
  "Main horizontal" 3 "select-layout main-horizontal"
  "Main vertical"   4 "select-layout main-vertical"
  "Tiled (grid)"    5 "select-layout tiled"
  "" "" ""
  "Move to session..." m "choose-tree -Zs -F '#{session_name}' \"move-window -s '#{window_id}' -t '%%'\""
  "Link to session..." K "choose-tree -Zs -F '#{session_name}' \"link-window -s '#{window_id}' -t '%%:'\""
  "Break all panes → windows" E "run-shell '$HOME/.config/tmux/break-all-panes.sh'"
  "" "" ""
  "Kill window" X "kill-window"
  "Renumber windows" N "run-shell 'tmux move-window -r && tmux display-message \"Windows renumbered\"'"
  "Rename"      n "command-prompt -F -I '#W' \"rename-window -t '#{window_id}' '%%'\""
  "" "" ""
  "⭐ Star"     s "run-shell '$HOME/.config/tmux/toggle-bookmark.sh \"#{window_id}\" \"⭐\"'"
  "📌 Pin"      p "run-shell '$HOME/.config/tmux/toggle-bookmark.sh \"#{window_id}\" \"📌\"'"
  "🔖 Bookmark" b "run-shell '$HOME/.config/tmux/toggle-bookmark.sh \"#{window_id}\" \"🔖\"'"
  "🚩 Flag"     f "run-shell '$HOME/.config/tmux/toggle-bookmark.sh \"#{window_id}\" \"🚩\"'"
  "Clear agent status" c "set-option -w -t '#{window_id}' -u '@workmux_status' ; display-message 'Cleared @workmux_status on #{window_index}:#{window_name}'"
  "" "" ""
  "New window"  w "new-window"
)

exec tmux display-menu -T "#[align=centre]#{window_index}:#{window_name}" -x R -y P "${rows[@]}"

  "New session" s "new-session"

  "" "" ""
  "Kill session"        X "kill-session"
  "Kill session & exit" E "run-shell '$HOME/.config/tmux/kill-session-exit.sh'"
  "Kill all sessions"   Q "confirm-before -p 'Kill ALL sessions (tmux server)? (y/n)' \"run-shell '$HOME/.config/tmux/kill-server-clean.sh'\""
)

exec tmux display-menu -T "#[align=centre]#{session_name}" -x R -y P "${rows[@]}"

22	  "Kill session & exit" E  "confirm-before -p 'Kill session #S and exit tmux? (y/n)' \"run-shell '$HOME/.config/tmux/kill-session-exit.sh'\""

25	  # the just-closed sessions on the next tmux start. See:

28	)

33	# N-new, x-kill etc.) is unaffected.
34	if [ -x "$HOME/.config/tmux/tmux-session-summary-popup.sh" ]; then
35	  rows+=(
36	    "" "" ""
37	    "AI session summary" u "display-popup -E -w 90% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' AI session summary ' '$HOME/.config/tmux/tmux-session-summary-popup.sh'"
38	  )

41	exec tmux display-menu -T " Session mgmt " -x R -y P "${rows[@]}"

1	# tmux — Keybindings
2	
3	All bindings use the default prefix `Ctrl + b`.
4	
5	## Daily Workflow
6	
7	| Keybinding | Action |
8	|------------|--------|
9	| `prefix + R` | Reload `~/.tmux.conf` |
10	| `prefix + Space` | Open the tmux popup menu (mnemonic: "menu") |
11	| `prefix + g` | Open sesh picker |
12	| `prefix + T` | Open sesh picker via television (tv) |
13	| `prefix + O` | Open sesh built-in picker |
14	| `prefix + S` | Jump to the last sesh session (status-bar message if none) |
15	| `prefix + 9` | Open `scode` for current dir (repo-aware coding-agent layout — nvim 75% \| agent 25% + btop monitor; idempotent, switches to existing session if already created) |
16	| `prefix + 0` | Lightweight sesh session at git root of current dir (no nvim/agent layout — symmetric counterpart to `prefix + 9`) |
17	| `prefix + N` | New session (prompts for name) |
18	| `prefix + X` | Kill session (with confirmation) |
19	| `prefix + W` | Kill window (with confirmation) |
20	| `prefix + r` | Renumber windows (close gaps left by killed windows) |
21	| `prefix + M` | Move current window to another session (prompts for `session[:index]`) |
22	| `prefix + B` | Break current pane into a new window and move it to a session (tab tear-out) |
23	| `prefix + A` | Link current window into another session (window appears in both) |
24	| `prefix + E` | Explode — break every pane in current window into its own window (same session). For switching from wide-screen multi-pane to mobile/SSH single-pane |
25	| `prefix + d` | Detach |
26	| `prefix + t` | Show tmux clock mode |
27	| `prefix + M-c` | Switch theme to Catppuccin (top status bar) |
28	| `prefix + M-t` | Switch theme to tmux2k (bottom status bar) |
29	
30	## Panes and Windows
31	
32	| Keybinding | Action |
33	|------------|--------|
34	| `Ctrl + 1..9` | Switch to window 1–9 (requires CSI-u terminal: Ghostty, Alacritty, Kitty) |
35	| `Ctrl + 0` | Lightweight sesh session at repo root for current pane (mirrors `prefix + 0`) |
36	| `Ctrl + h/j/k/l` | Move between panes — crosses into Neovim splits (vim-tmux-navigator)* |
37	| `Ctrl + \` | Focus previous pane/split (vim-tmux-navigator)* |
38	| `prefix + h/j/k/l` | Move between panes (fallback, tmux-only) |
39	| `prefix + H/J/K/L` | Resize panes (5 cells, repeatable) |
40	| `prefix + M-h/j/k/l` | Fine resize panes (1 cell, repeatable) |
41	| `prefix + +` | Set current pane to 75% width |
42	| `prefix + \|` | Split left/right (vertical divider) |
43	
44	\* `Ctrl + h/j/k/l` and `Ctrl + \` (vim-tmux-navigator) are gated on
45	the chezmoi `enableVimMode` prompt (default `true`). When `false`,
46	those bindings are omitted — `Ctrl+L` reaches the inner shell as
47	clear-screen, `Ctrl+H` as backspace, etc. Use `prefix + h/j/k/l` (kept
48	regardless) or `prefix + Arrow` for pane navigation. See
49	[`docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md`](../../this_repo/vim-mode.md).
50	| `prefix + -` | Split top/bottom (horizontal divider) |
51	| `prefix + c` | New window in current path |
52	| `prefix + x` | Kill pane (with confirmation) |
53	| `prefix + W` | Kill window (with confirmation) |
54	| `prefix + r` | Manually renumber windows (close index gaps) |
55	| `prefix + z` | Toggle pane zoom |
56	| `prefix + {` | Swap pane with previous (left/up) |
57	| `prefix + }` | Swap pane with next (right/down) |
58	| `prefix + m` | **Mark** current pane (built-in; one mark globally; needed by Join in menus) |
59	| `prefix + !` | Break current pane into a new window in same session (built-in) |
60	| `prefix + [` | Enter copy mode |
61	
62	`Ctrl+1..9` and `Ctrl+0` require CSI-u terminal support. Ghostty/cmux sends these natively. Alacritty needs explicit `keyboard.bindings` (managed by this repo in `dot_config/alacritty/alacritty.toml`). Legacy terminals (Terminal.app, plain SSH) cannot send these — use `prefix + number` instead.
63	
64	Swap-pane swaps the **content** while keeping the **sizes**. So if you have a 75%/25% split and swap, the left pane's content moves to the right (25%) and vice versa — the proportions stay fixed.
65	
66	## Layouts
67	
68	| Keybinding | Action |
69	|------------|--------|
70	| `M-1` | Even horizontal layout |
71	| `M-2` | Even vertical layout |
72	| `M-3` | Main horizontal layout |
73	| `M-4` | Main vertical layout |
74	| `M-5` | Tiled layout |
75	| `prefix + E` | Spread panes evenly (built-in) |
76	
77	`M-1` through `M-5` are tmux built-ins — no prefix needed; just hold Meta (Alt/Option) and press the number.
78	
79	> **macOS terminal requirement**: Option must send Meta/Esc+ for `M-` bindings to work. Ghostty/cmux: `macos-option-as-alt = left` (managed by this repo in `dot_config/ghostty/config`). Alacritty: `window.option_as_alt: OnlyLeft`. iTerm2: Profiles > Keys > Left Option Key > Esc+. See [docs/tools/ghostty.md](../ghostty.md).
80
```
